title: Real-Time AI-Driven Energy and Flexibility Management for a Technical Virtual Power Plant
abstract: This paper presents an AI-powered framework for real-time energy and flexibility self-scheduling of a technical virtual power plant (TVPP). The TVPP integrates electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs), energy storage systems (ESSs), photovoltaic (PV) panels, wind turbines (WTs), and distributed generators (DGs) to participate in wholesale energy and flexibility markets while adhering to distribution network constraints. The framework employs a two-stage approach to maximize profitability. In the first stage, a deep learning model forecasts short-term flexibility requirements. In the second stage, optimization is divided into two interdependent sub-problems. The first sub-problem coordinates EVCS and ESS operations through multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL), using multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO) with centralized training and decentralized execution (CTDE). The second, formulated as a linear programming (LP) problem, addresses the remaining system-level operations and constraints. These sub-problems interact iteratively through a feedback mechanism to align local decisions with global objectives. To enhance training efficiency, single-agent policies are pre-trained using proximal policy optimization (PPO) in simplified environments and later fine-tuned via transfer learning in the full MADRL framework. The proposed method is evaluated on the IEEE-33 bus test system, demonstrating superior operational efficiency and profitability over existing approaches.

title: PQMFA: Lightweight and Provably Secure Post-Quantum Multi-Factor Authentication Key Exchange Scheme for Smart Grid
abstract: The smart grid (SG) couples power infrastructure with pervasive communication and automated control, but this connectivity enlarges the attack surface of metering and communication links. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is therefore essential to prevent impersonation and unauthorized access. However, most MFA schemes rely on classical hardness assumptions and may not withstand quantum attacks. Moreover, SG terminals often operate under asymmetric resources and stringent latency constraints. Hence, it is urgent to develop post-quantum MFA schemes that are both secure and efficient, and practically deployable in SG environments. To ensure secure smart-grid communications in the post-quantum era, we propose a lattice-based lightweight and provably secure multi-factor authentication key exchange scheme (PQMFA). PQMFA integrates MFA into a lattice-based key exchange framework and leverages techniques such as fuzzy verifiers and honeywords to effectively resist password guessing attacks. Additionally, a novel lattice-based asymmetric computation method is introduced to reduce the computational overhead for smart meters. The security of PQMFA is formally proven under the Real-Or-Random (ROR) model. Comparative analysis with benchmark schemes demonstrates that PQMFA not only achieves strong resistance against various known attacks and ensures three-factor security, but also strikes a practical balance between security and efficiency.

title: An End-to-End Learning Model with Quantization Technology for Dynamic Prediction-Decision Joint-Making in Active Distribution Networks
abstract: Efficient load management and system stability in active distribution networks (ADNs) depend heavily on accurate load forecasting and dynamic decision-making. This paper proposes a novel end-to-end joint learning model for dynamic prediction-decision joint-making in active distribution networks. The model integrates a prediction module, leveraging long short-term memory networks to forecast photovoltaic (PV) generation, active power load, and reactive power load, with a control decision module based on Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3). The forecasting outputs are fed into the decision-making module, enabling dynamic adjustments to network parameters. A feedback mechanism is introduced that incorporates decision losses into the prediction module to enhance forecasting accuracy, thereby creating a tightly coupled, end-to-end joint optimization framework. In addition, a mixed precision quantization technology is adopted to reduce computational overhead and facilitate efficient deployment. Experimental results on distribution networks demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms other methods in terms of load forecasting accuracy and dynamic control effectiveness, resulting in substantial improvements in the operational efficiency and stability of ADNs.

title: Smart Meter Scheduling for Data-Driven Granular Customer Voltage Visibility
abstract: The integration of distributed energy resources (DERs) in power distribution systems introduces greater voltage volatility. Supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) measurements at medium-voltage (MV) networks cannot directly monitor customer-end voltages; smart meters provide direct customer-end voltages but have insufficient reporting rates to track short-term voltage fluctuations due to DERs. This paper proposes an approach to high-resolution voltage monitoring at all customer points based on low-resolution smart meter measurements. This is based on staggered smart meter data acquisition: smart meters are grouped into subsets, each of which contains enough information to estimate the voltages of all customers. These subsets of smart meters are scheduled to report their data at different times rather than simultaneously. Then, at each instant when a subset of meters reports their measurements, a data-driven method is used to estimate all the unreported customer voltages by utilizing voltage measurements of the reporting subset. To support multi-customer estimation with minimal computational overhead, an eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model is chosen due to its efficiency and robustness. This approach ensures high-resolution voltage estimation (HiVE) without the need of increasing the reporting rate of smart meters. Extensive simulations on real-world smart meter datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Large Language Model-based Smart Agents for Attack-Defense Game on Cyber-Physical Power Systems
abstract: With the deep integration of information technology, cyber-physical power systems (CPPSs) face increasingly complex attack-defense challenges. Traditional game theory-based methods struggle with sophisticated strategy reasoning and decision interpretability. This paper proposes an innovative CPPS attack-defense game paradigm incorporating large language model (LLM)-based smart agents to address these limitations. First, we define a game model integrating Bayesian Nash Equilibrium and betweenness centrality to characterize the strategy stability and key node prioritization. Second, we design smart agent architectures with memory, toolset, planning, and action execution modules to enable adaptive strategy formulation in complex environments. Then, we give a systematic elaboration of the dynamic game processes, including vulnerability scanning, attack, detection, response, and post-analysis phases. Experiments on IEEE 14 and IEEE 33 bus systems demonstrate that the proposed method significantly enhances defense success rate, convergence efficiency, and strategy diversity, validating the potential of LLMs in improving CPPS security through the intelligent attack-defense game.

title: Unsupervised Lightweight Transfer Learning for Edge Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring
abstract: Non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) is crucial for residential real-time energy management as it provides appliance-level consumption insights. Deploying NILM at the edge enables immediate feedback and preserves user privacy by processing data locally. While deep learning has significantly advanced NILM, its direct deployment on the edge faces major hurdles. The deep learning models are often too large to be applied to resource-constrained hardware. In addition, their performance may degrade substantially for a new household due to cross-household domain shifts. To overcome these two obstacles, this paper presents a novel lightweight transfer learning framework consisting of two main phases: dynamic network compression (DNC) and lightweight cross-domain transfer (LCT). DNC enables the progressive shrinking training of an elastic supernet in the cloud, which can be flexibly compressed into compact subnets tailored to the memory constraints of various edge devices without retraining. LCT enables efficient fine-tuning of deployed subnets at the edge in an unsupervised manner, adapting them to locally unlabeled cross-domain data by only updating lightweight residual modules. Experiments on a hardware testbed demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms existing methods in both disaggregation accuracy and memory efficiency, demonstrating its capability to deliver high-performance NILM on various edge devices.

title: Optimal Distribution of Grid-Following and Grid-Forming Converters for Charging Control of Electric Vehicles
abstract: We address the problem of determining the optimal combination of grid-following (GFL) versus grid-forming (GFM) modes of control in electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs) to maintain an acceptable balance between small-signal stability and voltage stability of electric distribution grids. We recall the state-space dynamic models of EVCSs operating in GFL and GFM modes and demonstrate how high charging rates of electric vehicles (EVs) in the GFL mode can impact small-signal performance. We then optimize the GFL-to-GFM ratio while also determining the optimal EV charging setpoints and a state-feedback controller to minimize the  $\mathcal {H}_{2}$ -norm of the grid transfer function (TF). To make the proposed optimization computationally favorable, we use participation factor analysis to identify the most dominant EVCSs in the GFM mode so that they can be prioritized for optimization. We validate our results using a modified model of the IEEE 33-bus power distribution test system with ten EVCSs.

title: Multi-Period Operation of Power-Transportation Networks With Multiple Stakeholders: A Generalized Nash Equilibrium Method
abstract: The rapid proliferation of electric vehicles (EVs) is strengthening the coupling of transportation and power networks. Both electricity prices and traffic conditions can affect EV users’ traveling and charging decisions, leading to complex interactions among various stakeholders across the two networks. This paper proposes a generalized Nash equilibrium-based method for multi-period coordinated operation of the coupled power-transportation network (CPTN) with different stakeholders. First, a multi-period decision-making model of vehicle users is established, which captures users’ flexible travel and charging demands. Then, to alleviate both power and traffic congestion, a pricing scheme is incorporated to adjust the nodal electric netload and the transportation link flow in the coupled network. Finally, the coordinated operation problem of CPTN is modeled as a generalized Nash game, which is further reformulated into variational inequalities. A modified projection-contraction algorithm is presented to obtain the equilibrium point. Simulation results demonstrate that compared with the operation method without pricing schemes, the proposed one can effectively reduce both network losses and total travel time under various conditions. The proposed vehicle user model can capture the multi-period flexible travel and charging demands, enabling users to balance time, economic, and discomfort costs.

title: Triple-Stage Collaborative Optimization Method for Cross-Regional Data Centers Considering Optimal Coalition Matching
abstract: With the rapid advancements of artificial intelligence, cross-regional collaboration among data centers (DCs) has emerged as an effective strategy to enhance resource utilization and reduce energy consumption. Without such collaboration, DCs may experience higher operational costs and energy consumption due to imbalances in computational load and disparities in regional electricity prices. Therefore, a triple-stage collaborative optimization method for cross-regional DCs considering optimal coalition matching is proposed. In Stage 1, a potential coalition search method for DCs is proposed, and the Bron-Kerbosch pivoting algorithm is employed to identify high-quality potential coalitions under multi-dimensional complementarity. Then, an optimal collaborative operation model for DCs incorporating fine-grained cooling system modeling is established in Stage 2, aiming to jointly optimize computational load scheduling and energy management. Based on this, an optimal dynamic coalition matching mechanism for DCs is proposed in Stage 3, integrating a rolling-horizon control strategy to adaptively update coalition structures and operation strategies under varying fluctuation levels. Case studies on ten heterogeneous cross-regional DCs demonstrate that the proposed method effectively reduces energy consumption, increases coalition profits and member satisfaction, thereby enhancing both economic performance and operational stability.

title: Inner-Product Based Detection of Cross-Line Successive Single-Phase-to-Ground Faults in Resonant Active Distribution Networks
abstract: Existing protection schemes often fail to detect cross-line successive single-phase-to-ground (SSPG) faults in resonant-grounded active distribution networks, due to the severely weakened transient signature that results when a secondary fault (f2) superimposes on an uncleared primary fault (f1). To address this, a novel detection method based on inner-product analysis is proposed. First, a transient equivalent circuit for the f2 fault is established. Expressions for the transient zero-sequence currents in healthy, primary, and secondary fault feeders, as well as for the bus zero-sequence voltage, are subsequently derived and analyzed. Then, the inner-product is applied to reveal the inherent correlation between healthy and faulty feeders during an f1 fault. For the f2 fault, distinct dynamic patterns, specifically in the amplitude and polarity of the inner products, are revealed for the primary, and secondary fault feeders. This analysis provides the theoretical foundation for SSPG fault detection. Furthermore, a differential preprocessing algorithm is introduced to enhance transient signatures, thereby improving the reliability of the inner-product based detection. Simulation and field test results confirm that the proposed method accurately detects both the f1 and f2 faults under challenging conditions, including short fault intervals, diverse grounding resistance combinations, distributed generation integration, arc faults, and strong noise interference.

title: Future Trajectory Representation-Aided DRL for Real-Time Battery Energy Storage Dispatch in Distribution Networks
abstract: Dispatching battery energy storage systems (BESS) in distributed grids is challenging due to the sequential nature of the decision-making process, which needs to account for future uncertainties in system states and time-coupling constraints. Numerous forecasting techniques have been developed to capture such uncertainties, but most prioritize accuracy alone, and their potential for enhancing optimization performance has rarely been studied. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a novel forecasting-aided deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based BESS dispatch approach that incorporates future trajectory representation into the DRL state space to facilitate more proactive decisions. Specifically, an error-free representation network is first trained offline using self-supervised contrastive learning to encode upcoming electricity prices, load demand, and renewable generation trajectories. It explicitly disentangles trend and seasonal patterns using a mixture of autoregressive experts and a learnable Fourier layer. During online control, the DRL agent receives both the current system state and the learned forecast representation, which are fused using a dynamic routing attention mechanism that adaptively balances present versus future information. The trajectory contrastive learning allows the proposed method to better capture the temporal dynamics of stochastic variables and generate representations that are easier for the agent to exploit. By incorporating structured predictive representations into the control loop, the proposed method can make more forward-looking charging and discharging decisions that consider future uncertainties. Extensive simulations on the IEEE 34-node and 123-node test systems demonstrate that the proposed method yields more cost-efficient BESS control policies compared to baseline approaches.

title: Faulty Feeder Detection Based on Quantitative Modulation of Ground Current in Active Flexible Grounding Systems
abstract: The increasing integration of distributed generations in active distribution networks introduces the dual-mode behavior in ground current amplitude, characterized by over-amplification or over-suppression. Conventional single phase-to-ground protection fails to actively reconstruct fault characteristics based on specific grounding conditions, which is difficult to take into account the sensitivity and security of fault detection. To solve the problem, this paper proposes an active quantitative modulation method of ground current to counteract the control of ground current in active distribution networks. Firstly, the mathematical models of ground current modulation under different active grounding types are established. Secondly, the optimal modulation target of ground current that takes into account both safe arc extinguishing and fault detection is proposed, and extract the ground current modulation information distributed in the fault line for faulty feeder detection. Finally, considering the unstable fault degree in the modulation process, a flexible transformation scheme of active grounding types is proposed to improve the adaptability of fault detection to random fault fluctuation. The effectiveness of the method is verified by simulation and the Changsha Jingke 10kV distribution network detection experimental platform.

title: Weather-aware Feeder Fault Prediction Based on Graph Learning with Synthetic Rare Event Generation
abstract: The increasing frequency and intensity of extreme weather events have significantly challenged the reliability of power distribution systems. Accurate prediction of weather-related feeder fault states under such conditions is hindered by two fundamental issues: (1) the mismatch between the Euclidean assumptions of traditional machine learning and the inherently graph-structured nature of distribution feeders, and (2) the severe class imbalance caused by the rarity of weather-related fault data. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a novel framework that integrates a graph convolutional network (GCN) with a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN). The proposed GCN-cGAN framework captures topological dependencies of feeders while synthesizing realistic rare fault events under extreme weather scenarios. A graph attention-based model is further developed for feeder fault prediction, leveraging both real and synthetic data samples. Extensive experiments on real distribution topology and meteorological data show consistent gains under multiple evaluation scenarios, including strong wind, heavy rainfall, and their combination, with marked robustness to class imbalance. Under the present prediction setting, compared with conventional and state-of-the-art baselines, Recall improves by about 28 percent and F1-score by about 21 percent.

title: Aggregate Model of Distributed Multi-Energy Flexible Resources for Power System Operation: A Decomposition Approach
abstract: Distributed multi-energy flexible resources (DMEFR) can exploit the complementarity of electricity, gas, and heat to enhance power flexibility, demonstrating significant potential to promote renewable energy consumption and improve operational economics. An accurate model describing the aggregate feasible region (AFR) of DMEFR is essential for power systems to leverage this flexibility effectively. However, the time-coupling characteristic of DMEFR results in a prohibitive computational burden when computing the exact AFR. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel decomposition-based aggregate modeling method for DMEFR that features high computational efficiency and clear physical interpretation. First, we prove that the AFR of DMEFR is equivalent to the Minkowski sum of two decoupled components: a time-decoupled component capturing power boundaries via linear programming, and a time-coupled component (TCC) characterizing storage dynamics. Second, for the TCC, we develop an adjustable homothetic polytope (AHP)-based method that jointly optimizes the basic homothetic polytope, scaling factors, and translating factors, reducing the conservatism of fixed homothetic polytope-based methods. Third, we formulate the AHP optimization as a bilinear problem and propose a block coordinate descent algorithm with a convergence guarantee for it. Case studies validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method.

title: Clean-ET: A Novel Electricity Theft Method Based on Clean Backdoor Attack
abstract: As an efficient energy management system, the smart grid has been widely adopted in areas such as power system dispatch optimization and energy internet development. However, false data injection attacks (FDIA) represent a major security challenge for electricity theft detection (ETD) models by manipulating data to mislead system decisions. Existing FDIA methods lack transferability, so the attack becomes ineffective once the defender changes the ETD model. Moreover, FDIA methods significantly degrade the classification performance of ETD models, increasing the risk of exposure and reducing stealth, complicating the demonstration of the potential threat of electricity theft (ET). In this paper, we propose a Novel Electricity Theft Method Based on Clean Backdoor Attack (Clean-ET) to highlight potential threats further. Clean-ET leverages inherent statistical differences in electricity consumption patterns and temporal periodic characteristics to stealthily embed a backdoor into the ETD model, facilitating covert electricity theft with strong cross-model transferability. Specifically, Clean-ET leverages the statistical differences in electricity usage between normal users and electricity thieves by incorporating Gaussian noise and temporal periodic cycle patterns. Moreover, we design triggers that seamlessly blend into the natural distribution of electricity data. This allows the backdoored ETD model to maintain high classification accuracy under normal conditions while misclassifying electricity theft cases under trigger conditions, enabling a long-term stealthy attack. Consequently, regardless of the specific ETD model used by the defender, our attack remains effective as long as the trigger samples are included in the ETD model training, highlighting the transferability of our attack. Experimental results demonstrate that under various parameter settings, our method attains an attack success rate (ASR) consistently above 80%, reaching up to 94%, while minimally impacting the classification performance of clean samples.

title: Scenario-Driven Deduction and Dual-Timescale Optimization Approach for Digital Twin of Hybrid AC/DC Microgrid
abstract: Hybrid AC/DC microgrids (MGs) are compatible with legacy AC grids and enable the integration of renewable distributed energy resources (DERs). However, emergencies such as unscheduled islanding expose a mismatch between day-ahead scheduling and sub-second dynamics. A digital-twin (DT) enabled dual-timescale framework is proposed that unifies upper-level optimal power flow (OPF) scheduling and lower-level model predictive control (MPC) via scenario-driven deduction in a bilevel formulation. Validated on an oil-and-gas well-station MG, the strategy issues consistent pre- and post-event process commands and preserves steady-state optimality. Relative to a second-order cone programming (SOCP) based OPF baseline, average AC frequency deviation and DC bus voltage deviation during islanding are reduced by 74.1% and 49.6%, respectively. Against two state-of-the-art methods, the tracking consistency between dispatched commands and measured transients improves by 23.8% and 31%. Computation for transient sequences completes within 6–10 s across scenarios, supporting real-time deduction on commodity hardware.

title: Accurate and Energy-Efficient Detection of Cyberattacks Against Non-Linear AGC Systems
abstract: Automatic Generation Control (AGC) systems are widely used in interconnected power systems. However, AGC systems fully rely on communicated measurements, making them susceptible to cyber threats, particularly False Data Injection Attacks (FDIAs), which can destabilize the grid. This paper proposes a novel Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs)-based deep learning (DL) framework for detecting FDIAs against AGC systems considering their nonlinearities. The proposed framework combines FDIA-detection accuracy and energy-consumption efficiency by integrating Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for feature extraction, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for temporal modeling, attention mechanisms for adaptive focus, and SNNs for energy-efficient computation. Three different variations of the proposed framework—an ANN-based DL model, a fully-spiking model, and a hybrid spiking-ANN-based model—are implemented and analyzed under a high-fidelity set of diverse FDIA scenarios against an AGC system with nonlinearities. Results demonstrate that the proposed Hybrid-SNN DL model can accurately detect FDIAs on AGC systems while reducing DL model’s energy consumption by up to 56%. These findings highlight the potential of SNNs for enhancing cybersecurity in smart grids, offering a sustainable approach to reducing operational costs.

title: Equilibrium Scheduling Strategy for MSOP via Bayesian Dynamic Segmentation of Complementarity among LVDNs
abstract: Mobile Soft Open Point (MSOP) technology improves the flexibility and utilization of interconnection resources by enabling mobile deployment across low-voltage distribution networks (LVDNs). However, efficient MSOP scheduling depends on accurately identifying the stage-wise complementarity among interconnectable LVDNs under time-varying source-load conditions. This paper proposes a bi-level equilibrium scheduling framework for MSOP by integrating stage-wise complementarity segmentation with coordinated scheduling optimization. First, a Gaussian mixture model is used to construct the complementary probability matrix among LVDNs, and Bayesian dynamic segmentation is employed to identify statistically stable complementarity stages from its temporal evolution. Then, by incorporating the segmented complementarity stages as stage-wise inputs, a bi-level MSOP scheduling model is developed to coordinate the trade-off between the net benefit of MSOP and the mobile scheduling cost. The scheduling problem is formulated as a Pareto-Nash-equilibrium-based multi-objective coordinated optimization problem. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: PI-YOLO: An Efficient Detector for Power Line Inspection using Aerial Images
abstract: Power line inspection, as a critical task of smart grid maintenance, has been empowered by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and neural detectors for automation and intelligence. The inspection task requires detectors to identify diverse equipment in high-resolution aerial images rapidly and accurately. However, existing detectors are still insufficient to meet these requirements, primarily due to their inadequate dataset scale, high-resolution adaptability, and network efficiency. To address these challenges, this paper first collects 99202 inspection images with a resolution of 4939×2987 and annotates 52 categories, thereby establishing the Power Inspection Unify Dataset (PIUD) as the data foundation. Then, PIUD is further processed by the proposed Power Inspection Multi-Scale (PIMS) framework to PIUD-MS to support high-resolution training and inference. Finally, this paper develops PI-YOLO based on YOLOv11 with improved performance in terms of multi-scale capability, network structure, and receptive field. PI-YOLO is publicly released as an efficient detector for inspection or annotation applications, whose advanced performance is validated by experiments on COCO, PIUD-MS, and InsPLAD. Compared with the baseline YOLOv11 and other detectors, PI-YOLO achieves both performance improvement and latency reduction. For example, PI-YOLO-Large improves AP by 0.7 while reducing latency by 1ms on PIUD-MS compared to YOLOv11.

title: Optimising P2P Energy Trading Using Internet of Things and Agentic AI Cluster Zooming
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become the game changer in smart grids-an enabler of network autonomy, self-healing, and reconfiguration. This study integrates AI and Internet of Things (IoT) to organise peer-to-peer (P2P) energy prosumers into virtual clusters without altering the physical topology of the power network. The aim is to enable an autonomous, scalable and dynamic virtual microgrids (VMG) by leveraging federated learning, agentic AI, AI agents, IoT, and cluster zooming to optimise P2P energy trading costs for prosumers and operational expenditure (OPEX) for network operators, depending on the number of prosumers available. The study employs a central controller AI to coordinate multiple local AI agents. Each AI agent resides in the network server and monitors energy trading traffic for each long-range wide-area network (LoRaWAN) gateway to optimise trading and OPEX costs via cluster zooming achieved by the spreading factor (SF) via adaptive data rate (ADR) mechanism of LoRaWAN. The agentic AI module in the cloud autonomously selects and adapts the network coverage based on SF, via the AI energy trading agent configured in the LoRaWAN access network server, to zoom the clusters (i.e., VMGs) in grid-connected and island modes. The study formulates an energy trading model connecting the physical (electrical) and virtual (telecom) distances and OPEX in the VMG. With agentic AI-assisted cluster zooming, over 70% of the energy is traded at lower SF. At the same time, the energy costs decrease by 40% in proportion to the network size and the number of prosumers. For the network operator, OPEX reduces by 21% and 38% in base-station power consumption. Ultimately, grid-connected prosumers pay higher charges than their off-grid counterparts. The agentic AI model in this study exemplifies a use case of the 3GPP model of the future 6G network.

title: Configuration of Distributed Wind-Storage System for Extreme Scenario of Distribution Network Under EV Participation
abstract: In order to solve the problem of voltage over-limit caused by high-permeability distributed wind power access to the distribution network, the optimal configuration of distributed wind-storage system for extreme scenarios of distribution network under electric vehicle (EV) participation is researched. Firstly, the uncertainty models of wind power output, load and EVs are established. Then, a large number of relatively complete source-load operation scenario data are generated by Monte Carlo, and an extreme scenario extraction method based on source-load balance entropy is established. Secondly, taking the wind farm as the cluster center, according to the voltage sensitivity index, a cluster division method based on the fixed cluster center is proposed. Then, considering the safe operation of the distribution network and the economic benefits of operators, a configuration model of self-configured energy storage (SCES) system of wind farms is constructed. Finally, the IEEE 33-node distribution network is used for example analysis. Compared with the existing configuration methods, it is found that using the proposed method the number of over-limit voltage is 0, and the network loss can be reduced by 48.23%. The proposed method can realize the optimal configuration of SCES capacity of each wind farm with EV participation, ensure the voltage stability of the distribution network in extreme scenarios, and improve the operation economy of the wind-storage system.

title: Distributed Secondary Control Based on Proportional-Integral Observers for Microgrids Under DoS Attacks and Encoding Mechanisms
abstract: Microgrids (MGs) are continuously evolving with the advancement of distributed energy storage devices and renewable energy generation. However, limited bandwidth and denial-of-service (DoS) attacks are threatening the stable operation of MGs by impacting data availability. By characterizing DoS attacks with attack frequency and duration, this paper pays attention to the secondary voltage restoration issue of a discrete MG by utilizing proportional-integral observers (PIOs) and dynamic encoding-decoding mechanisms (DEDMs). First, a local PIO with a predefined forgetting coefficient in its accumulative term is employed to estimate the states of the discrete-time MG, thereby mitigating the impact of DoS attacks. Subsequently, a consensus-based secondary controller is developed for the addressed system, leveraging the feedback linearization and PIO. DEDMs are implemented in communication channels to ensure efficient and reliable data exchanges. By resorting to the Lyapunov stability theory, sufficient conditions for voltage restoration are derived, taking into account the average dwell time and the proportion of attack silence. Moreover, desired observer and controller gains are calculated by solving a couple of matrix inequalities. Finally, a series of simulations based on Simulink are conducted to verify the practicality of the proposed controller.

title: A Tensor Decomposition Personalized Federated Learning Method for Distribution System State Estimation Considering Dynamic Impacts of Transmission Network
abstract: Traditional methods for distribution system state estimation are inadequate in capturing and coordinating the dynamic effects imposed by the transmission system. In addition, data privacy breach risks in power systems have become increasingly pronounced. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Tensor Decomposition Personalized Federated Learning (TDPFed)-based Dynamic-Static Integrated State Estimation (DSISE) method for the coordinated transmission-distribution (T&D) networks. A DSISE model is constructed where the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF)-based dynamic state estimation is for the transmission network, and the Generalized Maximum Likelihood approach based on Projection Statistics (GM-PS) for static state estimation is for the multi-area three-phase unbalanced distribution network. To reduce model communication costs and improve convergence speed, TDPFed designed a two-layer loss function to realize the decoupling between the personalized model and the tensor local model by controlling the distance. In addition, this paper also designs an efficient distributed learning strategy and model aggregation methods for TDPFed. Through theoretical analysis and experimental validation, it has been proven that the TDPFed-DSISE framework not only reduces communication costs but also significantly improves estimation accuracy compared to traditional federated learning algorithms.

title: Topology Change Estimation in Power Distribution Networks: A Machine Learning Approach
abstract: A critical component in distribution grid monitoring and control is the knowledge of the distribution network and the capability to detect and localize any topology changes, including line outages and additions, in near real-time. Traditionally, such a requirement is achieved with the breaker status and smart meter measurements. However, the slower data rate and inadequate wireless protection of such measurements degrade the situational awareness and make the system vulnerable to cyber-attacks. In this context, phasor measurement units (PMUs) are a robust and secure alternative, having a faster data rate and an integrated advanced cyber-protection mechanism. In this article, we propose a comprehensive solution to (1) detect physical topology changes, such as branch outages and additions, (2) detect change instants, and (3) localize the changes, entirely from phasor measurements, and without any prior information about the network. Furthermore, our proposed strategy can detect and localize multiple branch outages or additions, or a combination of both at the same time. We employ the expectation-maximization technique for change detection, and the outcome of the same is utilized in (1) a Kernel-density estimator module to detect change instants and (2) a data-driven topology learning technique to localize the changes. We perform real-time hardware-in-the-loop experiments on a modified IEEE 33-bus, 226-bus, and 1262-bus network emulated on a real-time simulator. Our experimental validation corroborates the utility and scalability of our proposed methodology.

title: Real-time Measurement of Transition Resistance and Full-time Fault Feeder Selection for Random Arc Fault in Active Distribution Networks
abstract: Single-phase-to-ground fault occurs frequently in active distribution network, often accompanied by nonlinear arc, and the fault development trend changes instantaneously and randomly. However, the existing fault detection methods for stable faults or specific arc faults are difficult to work in practical fault conditions. To achieve real-time tracking of the fault development trend, precise identification of fault types, and reliable selection of fault feeder for random faults occurring in complex and diverse environments, a novel method for real-time measurement of transition resistance and full-time fault feeder selection is proposed in this paper. Firstly, an equivalent circuit diagram of the active distribution network is established considering the parameter asymmetry and damping ratio, to acquire the current flowing through the transition resistance and the voltage across it in real time. Subsequently, the transition resistances of various types of faults are measured in real time based on Ohm’s law, and the stability, periodicity and mutation characteristics of the measured transition resistance are utilized to accurately identify the fault type and track its development trend. Finally, the zero-sequence current is decomposed to eliminate, as much as possible, components irrelevant to fault feeder selection. This process ensures that the characteristic waveforms of the fault feeder and normal feeders remain in opposite phases throughout the entire time period, thereby preventing selection failures caused by the loss of critical transient information. Simulation and 10kV experimental platform prove the feasibility of the proposed methods.

title: Demand Response Potential Evaluation for Commercial HVAC Loads Considering Cooling Storage in Chilled Water Loops
abstract: Commercial HVAC systems offer great potential for demand response (DR). Existing methods for HVAC DR evaluation often neglect the cooling storage effect within chilled water loops. However, this effect provides substantial flexibility and its omission leads to considerable underestimation of DR potential. Incorporating this effect poses major modeling and computational challenges due to the spatiotemporal variation of chilled water temperature and the complex coupled dynamics between chilled water loops and the indoor environment. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel method for evaluating HVAC DR potential considering cooling storage. First, we develop a model for chilled water loops based on 1-D advection-diffusion partial differential equations (PDEs). Then, a stepwise solution approach that leverages the identified stepwise rising pattern in chilled water temperature during DR events is proposed to solve the physical process effectively without directly solving the full PDEs. A high-fidelity simulation platform is established to validate the proposed method. Results indicate that, in most scenarios, the DR potential evaluated with the cooling storage effect is more than twice as high as that evaluated without it.

title: Personalized Dynamic Operating Envelope-Based P2P Energy Trading: A novel Multiagent Safe Reinforcement Learning
abstract: While the growing proliferation of distributed energy resources (DERs) promotes the local energy market to form a user-friendly peer-to-peer (P2P) trading mode, it also renders a physical network system security violation risk. To safeguard the safety network operation, this paper proposes a personalized dynamic operating envelop (DOE) based P2P energy trading clearing model, solved by a novel multiagent safe reinforcement learning (MASRL) method. During the operation horizon, prosumers configure the expected injection power by flexibly scheduling internal resources. Based on the expected injection power, the distribution system operator (DSO) would incorporate the Shapley value into the DOE computation scheme to ensure network integrity and reflect each prosumer’s marginal contribution to P2P trading. A state-wise cost function is introduced to quantify the deviation between the expected injection power and the personalized DOE assignment, thereby indirectly indicating the degree of network violation or potential safety margin. To meet the basic requirements of security network operation, a multiagent absolute state-wise constraint policy optimization (MAASCPO) algorithm is proposed to minimize state-wise cost while enhancing the economic benefits of P2P trading. Simulation results for distribution networks are illustrated to validate the effectiveness of the proposed model in terms of scalability, security, and financial benefits.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Driven Control for DC Solid State Transformer in DC Microgrid
abstract: The DC solid-state transformer (DCSST) serves as a key component for connecting power supplies, loads, and other elements in a DC microgrid system. With the integration of new energy sources and random loads, the system has become increasingly complex, making accurate modeling challenging due to high modeling costs. The randomness of the loads introduces various disturbances, compromising system stability. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a data-driven model-free control (DMFC) approach based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and an improved Kalman filter (IKF) for the DCSST. First, a data-driven model of the DCSST is established. Next, the IKF is designed, which is tailored for DMFC to correct measurement errors, filter noise, and estimate uncertain disturbances. Subsequently, the DMFC is introduced, which ensures stability under large signal disturbances without relying on an accurate system model. Finally, a DRL sub-controller is integrated into the DMFC to intelligently adjust the control signal and enhance the system’s operational adaptability. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed control method can adaptively ensure the stability of the system under large signal disturbances without requiring an accurate model, while also exhibiting good dynamic and steady-state performance.

title: Robust Observer-Enhanced Resilient Control of Grid-Following LCL Inverters Under Cyber Sensor Attacks
abstract: This paper presents a robust proportional–integral (PI) control strategy with an observer for grid-following (GFL) inverters modeled as cyber–physical systems (CPS), designed to withstand denial-of-service (DoS) and intentional electromagnetic interference (IEMI) attacks targeting sensors and controllers. Such attacks can corrupt sensor measurements, cause communication delays and outages, degrade control performance, and even destabilize the system. In contrast to existing control approaches, the proposed method explicitly mitigates the detrimental effects of both DoS and IEMI attacks. The observer and PI controller gains are co-designed using linear matrix inequality (LMI) based optimization, ensuring robust stability under attack scenarios. Control and estimation processes are implemented within a time-triggered framework to guarantee deterministic timing and enable rigorous stability analysis. Furthermore, a residual-based fault and attack detection scheme employing fixed thresholds and hysteresis is introduced to promptly identify and isolate compromised sensors or communication links. Once an attack is detected, the system switches to healthy measurements or substitutes observer estimates to preserve stable operation. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated through real-time hardware experiments and MATLAB/Simulink simulations using a laboratory-scale grid-connected inverter. The results demonstrate the method’s strong resilience and stability against IEMI and DoS attacks compared with conventional control strategies.

title: Hydraulic Transients and Thermal Dynamics Embedded Contingency Analysis of Integrated Electricity and Heating Systems
abstract: Intensified coupling between electricity and heating systems increases the risk of cascading failure, necessitating the contingency analysis in integrated electricity and heating systems (IEHS). However, current studies assume steady hydraulics and focus on the malfunctions caused by thermal fluctuations without justifying the simplification of hydraulics. Thus, this paper proposes a combined hydraulic transients and thermal dynamics modelling and simulation framework for IEHS contingencies, laying the basis for a more realistic electric-heating fault propagation analysis. First, we first present the detailed contingency models in IEHS across different timescales, including static power flow, dynamic thermal flow, and transient hydraulic flow. Then, a novel contingency simulation algorithm is tailored for heterogeneous partial differential equations (PDEs) of hydraulic and thermal systems in contingency analysis. Finally, we developed a comprehensive framework to evaluate the impact of cross-system contingencies and identified the crucial role of the hydraulic transient system (HTS) in security analysis. Case studies verify the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed simulation and modelling framework and reveal that the hydraulics could escalate the severity of faults more than assumed in the literature.

title: DeepLR: Deep Learning Assisted Load Redistribution Attack on Cyber-Physical Power System
abstract: In this work, we propose DeepLR, a data-driven Load Redistribution (LR) attack model on cyber-physical power systems. Prior attack models in this domain are fundamentally inadequate, as they fail to address or offer only partial/isolated solutions to the three critical challenges of effective attack modeling: (i) high computation time, (ii) reliance on confidential (complete/partial) topology information, and (iii) the need to manipulate all loads in the grid. Significantly diverging from prior attack models, this paper presents DeepLR, a Deep Learning (DL) assisted attack model designed to address these three critical challenges of effective attack modeling in a single unified framework. We first reformulate the conventional LR attack problem into a DL formulation, thereby eliminating reliance on confidential (complete/partial) topology information in real-time. Second, we propose a data-driven approach to identify a potential attacking region (characterized by fewer lines and loads), which enables attackers to focus exclusively on manipulating a subset of loads within this region rather than the entire grid. Through numerical experiments and comparative analysis with prior attack models, we demonstrate two critical findings: (i) an equally potent LR attack can be constructed without access to confidential topology information in real-time, and (ii) targeting the identified attacking region, even with fewer manipulations, results in a more severe impact on grid operations. The case study on the IEEE 14 bus system and the IEEE 39 bus system demonstrates the efficacy of the proposed DeepLR approach.

title: Risk-aware Economic Scheduling for Hydrogen-enabled Building Energy Systems Considering Extreme Weather Events
abstract: Hydrogen-enabled multi-energy systems (HMESs) have received much attention due to their low carbon emissions, high cross-sectoral/temporal/spatial flexibility, and black-start capability. However, their management under extreme weather events is particularly challenging due to the interacting multi-timescale dynamics of electrical-thermal-hydrogen subsystems, spatiotemporally coupled constraints, and large-scale mixedinteger decision variables. In this paper, we investigate a risk-aware economic scheduling problem for building-scale HMESs and aim to address all the above challenges. Specifically, by taking multi-timescale energy-coupled dynamics, extreme weatherinduced source-load impacts, priority-based load shedding, and mobile emergency energy resources (e.g., electric vehicles and hydrogen fuel cell vehicles) into consideration, we formulate a risk-aware economic scheduling problem with the aim of minimizing the weighted sum of expected operation cost and conditional value-at-risk by optimizing the ex-ante rental quantities of mobile emergency energy resources. To solve this large-scale mixed-integer programming problem, we propose an algorithm that combines a farthest-first traversal-based clustering method with an improved quantum-behaved particle swarm optimizer (QBPSO)-based decomposition method. Simulation results indicate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

title: Detection of Unknown Attack in Cyber-Physical Power Systems via Self-Supervised Cross-Layer and Cross-Temporal Consistency
abstract: Modern power grids are increasingly exposed to diverse cyber-physical attacks that originate in the cyber layer and disrupt physical operation. A critical defense challenge is to rapidly determine whether an attack has occurred and identify its type. To address this challenge, this paper aims to develop a generalized detection scheme capable of identifying multiple types of attacks, particularly unknown ones. It is first observed that, under normal operation, cyber-layer data and physical-layer states are consistent across layers and evolve smoothly over time, while attacks disrupt these consistencies. Building on this insight, a self-supervised Cross-Layer Cross-Temporal Contrastive Learning (CL-CTCL) framework is proposed, which employs a Graph Attention Network-Gated Recurrent Unit (GAT-GRU) encoder to capture spatial dependencies and temporal dynamics. Two complementary contrastive objectives are introduced: Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization (VICReg) for cross-layer alignment and Information Noise-Contrastive Estimation with Momentum Contrast (InfoNCE-MoCo) for temporal consistency. Residual deviations from these consistencies provide reliable attack fingerprints, enabling detection and classification of both known and unknown attacks. Experiments on an IEEE 118-bus cyber-physical testbed show that the proposed CL-CTCL achieves high accuracy on known attacks and generalizes well to unknown ones, outperforming baseline methods across standard metrics.

title: A Hierarchical Game-Decoupled-RL-Based Energy Flow Optimization Strategy for Cross-Regional Railway Integrated Energy System
abstract: To improve energy efficiency in electrified railways, this paper proposes a hierarchical game-reinforcement learning (RL)-based energy management strategy for cross-regional railway integrated energy systems (RIES). The framework divides wide-area coordination into two levels: primary energy flow absorption and secondary energy flow compensation. At the upper level, a complete-information static game model achieves rapid and consistent energy matching among traction substations through dominant-strategy equilibrium, enabling stable cross-regional coordination without iterative optimization. At the lower level, a decoupled RL algorithm governs the energy storage systems by separating independent and simultaneous compensation modes, while a distance-based sampling policy accelerates convergence and enhances learning efficiency. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed strategy ensures strict convergence and real-time adaptability, reducing total traction energy consumption by 16.31% and lowering regenerative braking energy losses to below 5%. These results confirm that the hierarchical game–RL framework effectively improves both energy efficiency and system interpretability of the RIES.

title: AI Data Center Load Forecasting: A Liquid Neural Network Approach
abstract: Unprecedented growth of AI data centers exhibit highly stochastic and bursty electricity demand profiles, with load ramps of several megawatts within seconds, posing significant new challenges for smart grid stability and operation. Such events can destabilize power systems if not properly addressed, under-scoring the need for forecasting methods tailored to emerging loads. Accurate short-term power forecasting provides great potential to enable grid operators to dynamically allocate resources, maintain frequency stability, and reduce reserve requirements in smart grid with emerging large loads. To reliably interconnect growing demand of AI compute into power grids, there is a strong need for accurately forecasting AI data center power demand. In this paper, we propose a short-term, data center-scale power forecasting framework for AI training and inference using Liquid Neural Networks (LNN). Evaluated on large language models’ power traces, our approach achieves higher accuracy with fewer neurons compared to classical deep learning models, offering a scalable, efficient, and utility-scale forecasting solution. This highlights the potential of LNN as lightweight, adaptive models to capture the dynamics of emerging large loads more effectively, thereby enabling grid operators to maintain reliability under increasing AI data center demands.

title: Linearized Optimal Power Flow for Multi-Phase Meshed Unbalanced Power Distribution Systems
abstract: Recent advancements in urban electrification have reshaped power distribution, yet most optimization research remains limited to radial feeders and simplified models that overlook the role of transformers and secondary networks—where most distributed energy resources (DERs) are connected. In practice, urban grids often feature heavily meshed secondary networks, creating challenges for accurate and tractable power flow optimization. Existing formulations for meshed networks are typically based on bus injection models and balanced assumptions, which hinder effective linearization and scalability. This paper presents a linearized branch flow model for unbalanced, multi-phase distribution systems with arbitrary topologies and detailed transformer representations. A unified linear meshed power flow (LM-PF) and optimal power flow (LM-OPF) formulation is derived for radial, weakly meshed, and heavily meshed networks, supported by new linearized angle recovery conditions. The proposed model explicitly addresses the trade-off between accuracy and tractability by providing theoretical error bounds and comparisons with existing nonlinear optimization (NL-OPF) methods. Extensive case studies were conducted on the radial and meshed IEEE 13-node feeder, the meshed IEEE 123-node feeder, and the heavily meshed IEEE 342-node feeder. These include: (i) power-flow validation under varying loading conditions, (ii) optimization-based comparison with the nonlinear OPF for cycle-constraint validation, and (iii) power-flow accuracy evaluation on networks with a large number of transformers under diverse loading scenarios. These results confirm that the proposed LM-PF, LM-OPF, and transformer modeling framework is highly accurate, scalable, and enables optimization-friendly formulations suitable for large-scale distribution system applications.

title: A Spatiotemporal Information Extraction-Based FDI Attack Detection and Data Recovery Architecture for Wind Power Prediction Systems
abstract: With the increasing penetration of wind energy in power systems, forecasting wind power has emerged as an effective method to enhance system stability. However, the accuracy of wind power prediction is significantly influenced by the quality of data collected by the wind farm’s communication system, which is vulnerable to cyberattacks. The inherent strong volatility of wind energy provides natural cover for false data injection (FDI) attacks, making their detection in wind power prediction systems a very challenging problem. This paper brings new insights into FDI attack detection and data recovery through spatiotemporal information extraction for wind power prediction systems. First, wind power time series data from multiple wind turbines are decomposed into trend, seasonal, and residual terms to provide additional spatiotemporal information for feature extraction. Subsequently, a novel extended long short-term memory autoencoder framework, incorporating k-fold cross-validation and z-score-based dual-threshold strategies, is developed to reconstruct these decomposition terms for accurately and iteratively identifying FDI attacks. Further, the compromised data is recovered using a spatiotemporal graph neural network with a dynamic trust weight mechanism. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve more accurate performance than existing methods.

title: Joint Robust and Chance-Constrained Optimization for Pre-Disaster Hardening Strategy of Power-Thermal Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: The integration of large-scale distributed photovoltaics (PVs) introduces significant operational uncertainties in urban power-thermal cyber-physical systems (PTCPS), particularly during typhoon events, which pose severe risks to system safety. Distribution-based models, such as chance constraints, effectively handle PV uncertainties. However, under extreme typhoon events, the scarcity of component fault data limits the availability of distribution knowledge, thereby reducing their effectiveness. To overcome this challenge, a joint robust and chance-constrained optimization (JRCCO) framework for pre-disaster coordinated hardening of PTCPS is proposed. The framework incorporates parameter distribution knowledge and uncertainty sets to minimize safety investment costs. Notably, multi-region sequential fault decision-dependent uncertainty (DDU) sets, designed to operate without requiring distribution knowledge, are introduced alongside chance constraints for PV output. To address the nonlinearity in chance constraints, a linearization method combining chance capacity and Cornish-Fisher series expansion is developed. Moreover, to improve computational efficiency and universality, a modified relaxed column-and-constraint generation with robust cuts (MRCCG-RC) algorithm is developed, which is complemented by acceleration techniques and supported by theoretical proofs. Two PTCPS of different scales are tested, showing that the strategy can reduce hardening costs by 19.15% and load shedding by 41.61%, effectively enhancing the PTCPS's performance against typhoon disasters.

title: V2G Coordination for Secure and Low-Carbon Operation of EV-Rich Distribution Systems: A Safe Reinforcement Learning Approach
abstract: The increasing popularization of electric vehicles (EVs) offers opportunities to reduce carbon emissions via vehicle-to-grid (V2G) coordination. This paper proposes a secure and low-carbon V2G coordination framework for EV fleets based on the proposed grid-interactive multi-region model (GMM), which characterizes realistic EV operation patterns (e.g., charging, discharging, and driving) impacted by complex V2G coordination and enables accurate impact analysis of EV aggregation on the EV-rich distribution system (ERDS). To effectively learn a secure V2G coordination policy in ERDS with infrequent voltage violation signals, a bounded PID (BPID) Lagrangian safe reinforcement learning (BPID-SRL) method is proposed, aiming to optimize carbon emissions without inducing voltage violations. A Transformer-GNN (TG) agent is then designed to jointly handle the spatiotemporal complexity of V2G coordination in ERDS, thereby enhancing the performance of the proposed BPID-SRL. A case study based on a modified IEEE 33-bus system empirically demonstrates the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed BPID-SRL and its big potential to exploit V2G coordination for secure and low-carbon operations of ERDS.

title: A Short-Circuit Calculation Method for Distribution Networks with 100% Converter-Based Generators Based on Outer-Layer Voltage Approximation and Inner-Layer Spectral Gradient Iteration
abstract: With the continuous advancement of power electronic equipment and the widespread integration of distributed generation, distribution networks composed entirely of converter-based generators have become one of the key development approaches for low-carbon and flexible modern distribution systems. This paper investigates a short-circuit calculation method for 100% converter-based generator distribution networks with system voltage established by V/f-controlled converters and multi-point grid-following distributed generation integration. The limitations of the widely used fixed-point iteration method in short-circuit calculations for active distribution networks are analyzed. The intrinsic relationships between the capacity of V/f-controlled generators, the capacity and connection locations of grid-following distributed generators, the magnitude of fault resistance, and the convergence behavior of the fixed-point iteration sequence are revealed. To address the convergence issues of traditional iterative algorithms caused by the capacity of converter-based generators and fault conditions, a short-circuit calculation method based on outer-layer voltage approximation and inner-layer spectral gradient iteration is proposed. The global convergence of the proposed method is mathematically proven. A case study involving a 100% converter -based generator distribution network with five converter-based generator nodes is conducted. A simulation model is built in PSCAD/EMTDC to simulate fault scenarios. The effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method are validated by comparing the short-circuit calculation results with simulation results and benchmarking against fixed-point iteration methods.

title: IGNN: An Inference Graph Neural Network for Data Sensitivity Assessment Considering Data Inference Leakage in Cyber-Physical Power Grid
abstract: Modern Cyber-Physical Power Grids (CPPG) rely heavily on fine-grained data exchange, yet they face the concealed threat of Data Inference Leakage (DIL), where attackers infer sensitive parameters from seemingly non-sensitive data. Existing risk assessment methods typically focus on direct cyber-attacks or employ static binary classifications, failing to capture the dynamic risk propagation caused by complex physical and statistical data couplings. To address this, this paper proposes a unified data sensitivity assessment framework based on a novel Inference Graph Neural Network (IGNN). We first construct an inference relation graph that integrates both model-driven and data-driven correlations. An analytic hierarchy process (AHP) model is constructed to calibrate the intrinsic sensitivity baseline. Subsequently, a novel inference-weighted Graph Attention Network (GAT) is developed to quantify the final sensitivity by aggregating the risk propagating through the inference pathways. Experiments on IEEE 30-, 57-bus, ACTIV 200-bus, and case 1354-pegase systems demonstrate that the proposed method effectively quantifies data sensitivity and identifies high-risk data susceptible to DIL, exhibiting strong robustness across different system scales. Quantitative results indicate that the high-sensitivity data identified by our method yield a highly threatening inference accuracy of up to 0.9145, significantly outperforming GCN-based and rule-based benchmarks.

title: A Cross-Line Successive Fault Detection of Distribution Network Based on Zero-Sequence Capacitance Variation
abstract: In non-effectively grounded system, the rise in phase voltage during single-phase grounding (SPG) fault poses a significant threat to the system’s insulation integrity. The increasing cabling rate in distribution network has led to a rising proportion of cross-line double successive single-phase grounding (SSPG) faults triggered by initial fault. To address the challenges of weak characteristic and difficult detection of such successive fault, this paper proposes a SSPG detection method based on zero-sequence capacitance variation. First, the dynamic zero-sequence equivalent network during successive faults is simplified, and derive the zero-sequence current (ZSC) expressions for each feeder under both overdamped and underdamped conditions. Subsequently, the singular value decomposition-total least squares extended Prony algorithm is employed to fit the zero-sequence voltage (ZSV) and ZSC, enabling the calculation of zero-sequence capacitance for both initial and successive faults in the complex frequency domain. A detection criterion is then constructed using the variation of capacitance. Finally, digital simulations and recorded field data validate the correctness and feasibility of the theoretical analysis.

title: Universal Graph Convolutional Network: Zero-Shot Transfer Across Power Grid Topology Reconfigurations
abstract: This work addresses a fundamental challenge in applying deep learning to network topology-dependent power system applications: developing neural network models that transfer across significant system changes, including networks with entirely different topologies and dimensionalities, without requiring training data from unseen reconfigurations. We focus on situational awareness tasks where predictions inherently depend on network-wide spatial relationships through electrical connectivity. Despite extensive research, most ML-based approaches remain system-specific, limiting real-world deployment. This limitation stems from a dual barrier. First, topology changes shift feature distributions and alter input dimensions due to power flow physics. Second, reconfigurations redefine output semantics and dimensionality, requiring models to handle configuration-specific outputs while maintaining transferable feature extraction. Our core insight is treating topology as a learnable dimension through training on diverse reconfigurations, enabling the model to learn universal power flow physics rather than memorizing fixed networks. We achieve this through three synergistic mechanisms: scalar-weight graph convolutions with physics-aware operators handle variable input dimensions and distribution shifts, adaptive pooling maps topology-specific features to unified latent representations, and parallel transformer generates configuration-specific outputs using positional encoding. Our Universal Graph Convolutional Network (UGCN) achieves transferability to any reconfiguration or variation of existing power systems without any prior knowledge of new grid topologies or retraining during implementation. Experimental results on state forecasting and false data injection detection demonstrate that UGCN significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in cross-system zero-shot transferability across both transmission and distribution networks.

title: Data-Driven Koopman Lyapunov Framework for Certified Region of Attraction Estimation of VSGs
abstract: The modern power grid is undergoing a major transition as converter-interfaced renewables and grid-forming virtual synchronous generators (VSGs) are increasingly deployed at scale. Region of attraction (ROA) estimation is effective for analyzing large disturbance dynamics in such converter-dominated systems, but conventional model-based methods are often conservative and more difficult to apply when voltage control dynamics are included. In this paper, we propose a data-driven Koopman Lyapunov framework for certified ROA estimation of VSGs. In the offline training phase, a spectrally regularized Koopman operator, conditioned via feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM), is learned to realize linear evolution in the observable space across diverse operating conditions, thereby encouraging a better-conditioned and more dissipative latent spectrum. In the online ROA estimation phase, a branched Koopman neural Lyapunov function is constructed with Koopman eigenfunctions as the core and a lightweight convex neural branch. Approximation errors in the learned Koopman operator are handled through the Koopman neural Lyapunov function, supporting certified ROA estimation with respect to the learned dynamics. Case studies demonstrate less conservative ROA estimates and broad applicability across varying VSG conditions. Code is available at https://github.com/dAngelo1208/dko tsa vsgs.

title: Data-driven Microgrid Operation Towards Optimized Battery Energy Storage Lifetime Degradation
abstract: This paper proposes a new data-driven approach for two-stage operation of a microgrid (MG) towards optimized battery energy storage (BES) lifetime degradation. At the first stage (day-ahead), the BES degradation range over the scheduled day is optimally allocated under day-ahead forecast of random variables. To accurately quantify BES degradation under temperature impact, a convex BES electrothermal-aging model is constructed. Then, a dynamic model constraint coefficient determination method is proposed for optimizing BES lifetime degradation using the historical operation and updated current information. At the second stage (real-time), an approximate dynamic programming method is developed to real-time optimize the MG operation after multiple uncertainties are realized. Considering the temperature dependent constraints of BES, a sequential decomposed value function slope update method is designed for enhanced optimization feasibility, BES aging quantification accuracy, and training efficacy, which can deliver high-quality solutions under uncertainties. Case studies on a MG system demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: A Spherical Manifold-Based Optimization Method for Coordinated Operation of Active Distribution Network With Networked Microgrids
abstract: For the active distribution network (ADN) with networked microgrids (MGs), it involves both discrete devices (e.g. tap changers and capacitor banks), and continuous resources, such as inverter-based distributed energy resources (DERs) and static VAR compensators. This makes the coordinated multi-period joint active and reactive power dispatch (C-MP-ARPD) problem a bilevel mixed-integer nonlinear programming (bilevel-MINLP) one. Nevertheless, research on the bilevel coordinated optimization problems with binary variables at each level is extremely limited. To fill this research gap, this work proposes a spherical manifold-based optimization method for the C-MP-ARPD problem. Specifically, the  $l_{2}$ -box method is employed to transform the bilevel-MINLP problem into a bilevel Riemannian nonlinear programming problem within the continuous domain. Then, a manifold-based model decomposition strategy is proposed, obtaining relaxed subproblems, box-subproblems and sphere-subproblems of both ADN and MGs, which can be efficiently coordinated by the enhanced manifold-based ADMM algorithm. Besides, a Riemannian trust-region method is employed to solve sphere-subproblems efficiently. Moreover, the bilevel relaxed subproblem of ADN and MGs is further equivalently decomposed into several small-scale subproblems by exploiting the spatio-temporal structure. Correspondingly, a hierarchical spatio-temporal decomposition method is developed to efficiently coordinate those obtained subproblems in a fully distributed and parallel manner. Finally, by integrating the aforementioned methods, a spherical manifold-based optimization approach is proposed for solving the C-MP-ARPD problem. The accuracy, computational efficiency, and convergence performance of the proposed method are verified through comparison with the commercial MIP solver Gurobi, as well as other representative distributed methods.

title: Duty-Cycle-Controlled Sub-Milliwatt Measurement Unit for Battery-Free Single-Frequency Injection Topology Identification
abstract: In single-frequency injection topology identification, a low-amplitude diagnostic tone (e.g., 833 Hz) is superimposed onto the network, and the widespread deployment of battery-free measurement units enables detection of the injected signal. Each node operates under strict power constraints, typically on the microwatt level, which limits raw waveform transmission. As a result, amplitude and phase information must be extracted locally. Furthermore, improvements in front-end noise characteristics can be exploited by the lock-in amplifier to achieve proportional reductions in the amplitude of the injected diagnostic current, thereby substantially mitigating network perturbations. We therefore present a system-in-package lock-in amplifier that dissipates 30.6 μW at 3.3 V and is tailored to demodulate an 833 Hz probe signal for distribution-grid topology identification. The circuit employs a duty-cycle-controlled multiplier with enable/disable gating to suppress quiescent consumption, achieving an input-referred noise density of 1.3 μV/√Hz and an approximately 19% reduction in average power consumption to support battery-less operation. This work thus establishes a field-deployable, maintenance-free sensing platform for large-scale topology monitoring and other energy-constrained applications, such as fault prevention and condition diagnosis in power networks.

title: Power Oscillation Mitigation of Inverter-Interfaced Distributed Energy Resources in Microgrids under Unbalanced Faults
abstract: Three-phase four-wire Inverter-Interfaced Distributed Energy Resources (3P4W-DERs) offer significant advantages, including reduced emissions, localized energy production, and enhanced reliability for modern power systems. However, during unbalanced fault conditions, 3P4W-DERs may generate oscillatory active and reactive power components. These oscillations lead to DC-link fluctuations, overcurrent stress on power electronic devices, and potential system instabilities. To mitigate these issues, this paper proposes a Triple Current Controller (TCC) based on positive-, negative-, and zero-sequence components. The TCC is designed to eliminate instantaneous power oscillations while ensuring the generated current remains within safe operating limits, even under severe unbalanced fault conditions. The proposed method eliminates the need for complex sequence extraction techniques, thereby reducing control complexity. Also, a current limiting strategy is integrated into the controller to enforce peak current constraints during fault events. The proposed TCC is adaptive to both grid-connected and islanded modes of microgrid operation. Simulation results confirm the TCC’s ability to suppress active and reactive power oscillations without exceeding current limits under a wide range of unbalanced fault scenarios.

title: Behind-the-Meter PV Disaggregation with Copula-Constrained Bayesian Variational Autoencoder and Feature Clustering
abstract: A quantitative assessment of the uncertainty of behind-the-meter (BTM) PVs is critical for accurate forecasts, voltage control, and distribution system security. This paper proposes a novel distribution-constrained Bayesian variational autoencoder approach with feature-based clustering (DC-BVAE-FBC), to disaggregate BTM PV generation from net load data probabilistically. By incorporating Bayesian inference into the variational autoencoder framework, the approach accurately captures uncertainty in the disaggregation process. A significant advance lies in constraining the latent space of the BVAE using a Gaussian C-Vine copula, which models the target component’s distribution—either native load or PV generation, ensuring that latent samples align with real-world patterns, thereby enhancing disaggregation accuracy. A feature-based clustering (FBC) strategy is also proposed for group days based on meteorological factors influencing power consumption and PV output, enabling tailored DC-BVAE models for each cluster to optimize predictions. Validated with real smart meter data with BTM PVs from London Advanced Metering Infrastructure (LCL-AMI) and Pecan Street Inc. Dataport (PS-ND/PG), this methodology demonstrates superior performance over existing techniques, offering a robust solution for modern grid management challenges.

title: Secondary Frequency Control Through Serverless Cloud Computing for Active Distribution Networks
abstract: With the growing integration of distributed energy resources (DERs), many regulating entities, such as the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) in the USA, have initiated a notice of inquiry for the utilization of cloud services for power system operation, including ancillary grid services from DERs. Motivated by these initiatives, this paper develops a serverless cloud computing architecture for real-time secondary frequency control in active distribution networks (ADNs). A secondary frequency control architecture is developed along with an optimization-based controller for optimally dispatching the regulating units in response to automatic generation control (AGC) signals. The developed optimization is fully integrated with the proposed serverless cloud computing architecture, utilizing several Amazon Web Services (AWS) such as Lambda, IoT Core, and S3. The AWS cloud architecture communicates with a real-time digital simulator, which mimics an ADN, utilizing IoT devices like Raspberry Pi and several utility standard communication protocols such as MQTT and TCP/IP. To demonstrate the dispatch of regulating units using the proposed serverless cloud computing architecture—and to validate the performance of the developed optimization-based controller—a real-time model of an actual feeder from NV Energy (the largest utility in Nevada) is utilized. Furthermore, a grid response time analysis is conducted to enable proper sequencing of frequency regulation commands by predicting the actual response time of the grid. The results of accurately dispatching the regulating units in response to AGC signals validate the accuracy of the optimization, demonstrate the successful implementation of the proposed serverless cloud-based AGC, and set the stage for practically implementing the proposed solutions.
