title: A Fully Distributed Market Clearing Framework for Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading in Heterogeneous Virtual Power Plants
abstract: Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) are proposed to aggregate numerous small-scale prosumers to handle their barriers in participating in Peer-to-Peer (P2P) markets due to capacity requirements. However, market clearing in P2P energy markets with multiple VPPs is challenging because of VPP heterogeneity, communication resource constraints, and the coupling between intra- and inter-VPP markets. This paper constructs a market clearing framework for this scenery. The fully distributed P2P energy market is designed for inter-VPP market with high communication costs and the intra-VPP market with insufficient communication resources to release the communication burden, while other intra-VPP market apply the distributed framework. Under such a setting, through the reconstruction of the fully - distributed P2P energy market clearing problem based on distributed estimation, the P2P energy market clearing problem for multiple heterogeneous virtual power plants is constructed. A market clearing algorithm is developed based on the consensus ADMM and parallel ADMM to maximize the utilization of communication resources and improving communication efficiency. Furthermore, based on marginal cost pricing, the electricity prices in the heterogeneous intra-VPP markets and inter-VPP market are discussed. Finally, the convergence and scalability of the proposed algorithm and the effectiveness of the electricity price analysis are verified on the IEEE 37-bus and IEEE 123-bus test feeders.

title: Tractable Attack Detection with Robustness Certificate for Nonlinear Power Systems under Stochastic Disturbances
abstract: This article presents a tractable attack detection methodology for nonlinear power systems that reduces complexity while providing a formal certificate of robustness against stochastic power disturbances. The inherent nonlinearity of power system dynamics typically necessitates sophisticated detection algorithms, while stochastic disturbances (e.g., fluctuating renewables) may introduce unforeseen behaviors that obscure attack discernment. This leads to two primary challenges: (i) model-based methods offer strong analytical foundations but may suffer from high computational complexity and rely on prior assumptions about disturbance distributions (e.g., Gaussianity); (ii) data-driven methods address uncertainty using statistical properties of large datasets or empirical validation within neural network architectures, yet they may lack performance guarantees. To this end, we propose (i) a linear detector that encodes stochastic disturbances through quadratic constraints, transforming the robust design problem into a convex quadratic program (QP), thereby ensuring tractability, and (ii) a robustness certificate that provides probabilistic guarantees in unseen scenarios with a desired confidence, based on the behavior of the optimal solution in active constraints (i.e., constraints that are equalities at the optimum). Unlike existing methods, our detection approach leverages the optimality properties of convex optimization to deliver performance guarantees without depending on prior assumptions or large datasets. We validate our method on cyber attack detection in Automatic Generation Control (AGC) within a two-area IEEE 118-bus system.

title: Optimal Renewable Power Purchase Agreements for Data Centers
abstract: Data centers have become integral to contemporary infrastructure. However, their electricity demand significantly adds to global energy consumption, resulting in substantial electricity costs and carbon footprints. Power purchase agreements, when used as bilateral long-term contracts for procuring renewable energy, not only hedge against volatility in an electricity market to secure locked-in prices but also play a crucial role in reducing carbon emissions. This paper studies the strategy of a data center to sign such power purchase agreements, which encompasses an optimal agreement design problem (static) and an optimal signing timing problem (dynamic) to maximize long-term expected electricity cost savings. In particular, we develop a continuous-time stochastic process model for long-term market price evolution in an electricity market, alongside a power purchase agreement model comprising the starting time, contract term, contractual power supply, and locked-in price. These models enable a novel problem formulation for PPA signing, which further allows for a tractable solution via decomposition. We first fix an arbitrary starting time and explicitly analyze how to set the other three variables with the most expected total saving. We then propose a dynamic threshold policy that online identifies an optimal starting time based on real-time observations of market prices. The proposed strategy is extensively tested with simulation experiments to validate our theoretical analysis. Numerical results also provide additional insights–over 35% reduction in long-term total electricity expenditure can be made possible for data centers, as long as power purchase agreements are properly signed.

title: Fixed-Time Privacy-Preserving Distributed Coordinated Control for Grid-Forming and Grid-Following Inverters in Microgrids
abstract: As renewable energy integration continues to grow and microgrid (MG) systems become increasingly complex, it becomes critical to ensure system stability, security, and coordinated control among heterogeneous inverter types. This paper investigates the coordination among grid-forming inverters (GFMIs), grid-following inverters (GFLIs) under PQ control, and GFLIs under droop control. To address this problem, a communication layer based on the leader-follower consensus (LFC) architecture is established to enable information exchange among GFMIs, PQ-controlled GFLIs, and droop-controlled GFLIs. Building on this framework, a novel fixed-time privacy-preserving distributed coordinated controller is proposed by introducing a state decomposition mechanism. The proposed controller achieves fixed-time regulation of GFMI frequency and MG main bus voltage, ensures proportional active and reactive power sharing among all inverter types, and maintains the confidentiality of MG operational data. In comparison with existing studies, this work integrates the coordination of different inverter types, ensuring both operational efficiency and privacy protection, which has not been fully addressed in previous literature. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through real-time hardware-in-the-loop experiments.

title: Optimal PV Power Smoothing in Hydrogen–Battery Systems Using an Adaptive Equivalent Consumption Minimization Strategy
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power plant variability presents a significant obstacle to grid stability. Hybrid energy storage systems (HESSs), which integrate battery energy storage systems (BESSs) with hydrogen units (i.e., electrolyzers and fuel cells), offer a viable solution to mitigate PV fluctuations and minimize power curtailment. However, existing control strategies are typically rule-based or offline-optimized, lacking the capability to address critical real-time challenges such as nonlinear efficiency characteristics, response delays in hydrogen subsystems, excessive hydrogen consumption, and battery degradation while complying with grid codes. This paper introduces an adaptive Equivalent Consumption Minimization Strategy (ECMS) for real-time, optimal power sharing among hydrogen-BESS systems. The controller minimizes a composite cost function that integrates efficiency-aware dispatch using empirical efficiency curves, health-aware penalties for aggressive state-of-charge (SOC) reversals and hydrogen overuse, delay-resilient compensation for hydrogen subsystem response lags, and degradation-aware control via online BESS aging assessment. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy significantly improves ramp rate (RR) compliance and system longevity. Compared to benchmark techniques, the ECMS reduces BESS degradation by 50% and nearly eliminates RR violations while maintaining hydrogen demand satisfaction and ensuring smooth SOC recovery.

title: Coupling-Aware Aggregation of Multi-Zone HVAC Loads Under Uncertainty: A Two-Level Framework
abstract: Aggregating building heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) loads unlocks substantial demand-side flexibility for power systems. Yet multi-zone coupling creates intricate interdependencies and uncertainty propagation, complicating the quantification of aggregate flexibility. To address this issue, this paper proposes a coupling-aware two-level aggregation framework. At the building level, tailored Gaussian elimination and coordinate transformation techniques are employed to recast the high-dimensional thermal dynamics as an equivalent lower-dimensional analytical expression. This expression streamlines the subsequent aggregator-level stage by: 1) clarifying the propagation of zone-level uncertainties to the building-level interface, 2) decoupling intra-building multi-zone coupling from inter-building aggregation, and 3) providing full-dimensional building-level flexibility sets that enable tractable reformulation. At the aggregator level, existing geometric aggregation approaches are generalized by a newly developed matrix-transformation technique. This technique effectively constructs inner approximations between polytopes of different dimensions, producing closed-form images of high-dimensional multi-zone HVAC flexibility in power subspace. The resulting inner approximation is then recast as a customized separatable linear program that efficiently determines the optimal aggregate parameters. Case studies validate the effectiveness of our framework, highlighting its accuracy, reliability, and scalability.

title: Adaptive Inertia of DC-link Voltage Synchronization
abstract: DC-link voltage synchronization (DCVS) can be the virtual synchronous generator (VSG) strategy for grid-forming converter, but its virtual inertia configuration problem remains unsolved. Therefore, this paper proposes a universal adaptive virtual inertia strategy for DCVS. The desired virtual inertia adaptively decreases with the rise of DC-link voltage deviation (frequency deviation), which is entirely opposite to that of the traditional VSG ignoring DC-link voltage dynamic. To configure the desired adaptive virtual inertia, the AC frequency of the interfaced inverter is correlated with the energy stored in DC-link capacitor by the linear proportional and power-law logic. It can effectively alleviate the trade-off problem between DC-link voltage fluctuation and power angle overshoot under large power variation for better dynamic performance. Moreover, it can improve the dynamic performance (less DC-link voltage fluctuation) not in the cost of the steady-state performance (low-frequency-resonance suppressing capability) by not increasing the loop gain around the equilibrium point. The real-time simulation based on NI-PXI and power hardware-in-the-loop (PHIL) experiment validate its effectiveness and advantages compared to traditional methodology.

title: A Reinforcement Learning-Adapter Renewable Energy Forecasting Framework for Two-Stage Distribution Network Scheduling
abstract: With deepening renewable penetration, distribution-network operators must rely on high-quality forecasts to schedule distributed energy resources. However, most existing Prediction– then–Optimization (PTO) approaches rely solely on forecasted values as inputs, while overlooking the significant impact of the coupling between actual and forecasted values on operational costs. This limitation hinders the practicality and deployment of many decision-oriented methods in power systems. To address this issue, this paper investigates the two-stage scheduling problem of distribution networks and formulates it as a Coupled Prediction–then–Optimization (CPTO) problem. Then, we propose a RL-driven decision-focused framework that integrates a Generative Pretrained Transformer (GPT)-based forecasting module with an improved Actor–Critic Reinforcement Learning (RL) adapter. Specifically, a GPT-based forecasting model with task-adaptive loss is proposed to capture the temporal characteristics of renewable energy outputs. On this basis, an RL adapter is designed to learn a decision-focused policy that dynamically refines the base forecasts, thereby effectively reducing the actual operating cost of the distribution network. Case studies on the IEEE 33-bus, IEEE 141-bus and IEEE 570-bus systems demonstrate that, compared with best baselines, the proposed framework reduces operational costs by 2.20% , 2.28% and 1.80% respectively, thereby validating its effectiveness and superiority in terms of both economic efficiency and operational reliability.

title: Nonsmooth Decentralized Voltage Controller for Constrained Regulation of DC Microgrids With Constant Power Loads
abstract: This paper presents a novel decentralized voltage controller that enforces state constrains at all times and significantly enhances the transient response of DC Microgrid networks with constant power loads. The structure of the proposed controller ensures the existence of a positive invariant set under the solution of the dynamics, enforcing boundedness of each nodal voltage around a rated value. A rigorous analysis is presented to formulate sufficient conditions on the controller tuning parameters such that the boundedness property is guaranteed despite the time-varying nature of the nonlinear load demand. Closed-loop stability of the entire DC Microgrid with respect to desired reference points is analytically proven by employing a suitable Lyapunov function. This allows us to estimate the region of attraction of the desired equilibrium and obtain conditions under which system stability is ensured at all times. Furthermore, the structure of the proposed controller significantly improves the convergence rate of the closed loop system when compared with similar approaches in the literature. The theoretic results are verified in both experimental and power hardware-in-the-loop testing scenarios, while demonstrating fast voltage restoration in cases of load demand fluctuations and constrained regulation to the desired voltage References.

title: Dynamic Self-Triggered Load Frequency Control for Multi-Area Power Systems Under Non-Ideal Communication Environments
abstract: Multi-area power systems (MAPSs) consist of multiple area subsystems, exchanging power between each area to maintain a balance of supply and demand. With the introduction of communication facilities, traditional load frequency control (LFC) methods and event-triggered communication mechanisms may not be effective due to network-induced delays and external attacks caused by non-ideal environments. In this paper, a decentralized LFC algorithm with a novel dynamic self-triggered mechanism (DSTM) for MAPSs under non-ideal communication environments is proposed to ensure secure operation. The proposed DSTM employs a dynamic threshold, a rest time interval and an internal dynamic variable, which can extend triggering intervals and effectively avoid Zeno behavior. An  $H_{\infty }$  stability criterion and a co-design criterion are derived by a switching-based Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional. Comparison simulations and hardware-in-the-loop experiments verify the superiority and effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

title: Nodal Frequency Nadir Chance-Constrained Economic Dispatch Considering Contingency Frequency Service from Hydrogen Electrolysis
abstract: Providing contingency frequency services (CFSs) through grid-forming (GFM) converter-interfaced resources (CIRs) is a technically effective method for bolstering the frequency stability of low-inertia power systems. However, this approach often causes significant power curtailment or high capital investment. Moreover, the heterogeneous dynamic characteristics of CIRs and increasing uncertainty of renewable energy sources (RESs) renders system-level frequency metrics under deterministic conditions insufficient, necessitating the incorporation of uncertain nodal frequency nadir (NFN) to ensure comprehensive frequency stability. To address these gaps, this paper proposes a novel NFN chance-constrained economic dispatch framework, which leverages hydrogen electrolysis systems (HESs) as cost-effective sources of CFSs. The framework first establishes a synergistic operation strategy for integrated grid-following RESs and GFM HESs to enable efficient delivery of CFSs under stochastic contingencies. System-level power dispatch decisions and device-level CIR settings (i.e., control mode) are then co-optimized to minimize operation costs while ensuring both the system-level and node-level frequency stability. Finally, to overcome the computational burden of the nonlinear NFN chance constraints, a computationally tractable solution methodology is developed that leverages input convex neural networks with analytical sensitivity analysis and Benders decomposition methods. The effectiveness and scalability of the proposed approach are validated through numerical simulations on two test systems.

title: A Dynamic Voltage-Reliant Framework for Voltage Regulation Using Synchronous Condensers, SVCs, STATCOMs, Feeders Switching and Distributed Unit Commitment
abstract: Effective decrease in losses and bus voltage deviation within distribution grids can be attained using grid switching (GS), placement of capacitors (C), or optimal distributed units commitment (DU commitment), in which consumers play crucial roles in this optimization processes. However, simultaneously performing dynamic GS and DU commitment (DUC), as well as coordinating the reactive power output of dynamic devices such as synchronous condensers (SCs), static synchronous compensators (STATCOMs), and static VAR compensators (SVCs), can considerably improve the grid’s voltage profile and reduce power losses under fluctuating conditions. Also, accurate load modeling is fundamental for analysis, as the situation of continuously fluctuating loads with respect to voltage directly impacts the energy dissipation and voltage regulation. This, in turn, influences control of GS, SCs, STATCOMs, SVCs, and DUC. Since representing the load versus its components is actually significant, this paper presents a flexible dynamic mixed-integer binary framework to anticipate more confidant and secure coordinated controls for GS, SC, STATCOM, SVC, and DUC to regulate the system’s voltage. The study is conducted on an example 14-bus distribution network and the standard 33-bus grid via the mathematically formulating components of load versus type of consumer along with reactive and active power generation based on voltage fluctuations. The findings demonstrate appropriateness of the presented framework for regulating voltage in distribution systems.

title: Quantal Response-Based Adversarial Reinforcement Learning for Smart Grid Attack-Defense Game with Bounded Rationality Evolution
abstract: Smart grids enhance power transmission efficiency through integrated cyber-physical systems, but simultaneously increase vulnerability to unexpected contingencies and malicious attacks. Adversarial reinforcement learning (ARL) has emerged as a promising technique for grid attack-defense games, however, existing methods assume attackers’ complete rationality, forcing defenders to engage in complex saddle-point optimization problems (i.e., solving for worst-case Nash equilibrium). Such an issue not only leads to over-conservative defenders, but also poses severe convergence challenges. To mitigate these problems, this paper proposes a novel quantal response-based ARL (QR-ARL) method. QR-ARL generalizes ARL into bounded rationality via entropy regularization, which helps reflect realistic attacker behaviors and reduce defensive conservatism. Building on this, a novel self-paced learning technique is then tailored to manage training complexity by adaptively evolving the attacker’s rationality. Additionally, to address the potential conflict between short-term control costs and long-term stability objectives, a parameter space perturbation technique is proposed to promote exploration and reduce the agent’s reliance on local reward signals. Numerical experiments on IEEE 39-bus and 118-bus systems confirm the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed method over existing ARL methods.

title: Vulnerability Analysis of Multi-Timescale DC Microgrids under False Data Injection Attacks
abstract: This paper presents a vulnerability analysis for the multi-timescale DC microgrid (DCmG) against false data injection (FDI) attacks. Using singular perturbation theory, the system dynamics are decomposed into a fast boundary layer subsystem and a slow reduced-order model. Sufficient stability conditions for both subsystems are derived, and input-to-state stability (ISS) of the slow subsystem is established under attacks. Furthermore, a zonotopic reachability analysis is performed to estimate the worst-case state deviation and compute an analytical admissible attack indicator for safety assessment. Theoretical predictions are validated through both numerical simulations and full-hardware experiments. It is demonstrated that the multi-timescale property leads to new attack surfaces, and the analytical attack bounds are consistent with observed voltage deviations, which can effectively guide safe and secure control under cyber threats.

title: CarbonGPT: Meta Causal Graph-Enhanced Large Language Models for Carbon Emission Forecasting in Large-scale Power Distribution Networks
abstract: Carbon emission reduction has emerged as a global core development objective, where dynamic carbon flow perception serves as the critical foundation for low-carbon dispatch. However, the electrification shift of transportation carbon emissions caused by large-scale electric vehicle (EV) grid integration, coupled with the grid impact from renewable energy source (RES) volatility, poses unprecedented challenges for accurate carbon emission prediction. Although adaptive graphs and large language models (LLMs) can achieve carbon emission prediction for power distribution networks (PDNs) under data sparsity scenarios, the spurious cross-variable correlations derived from their adaptive topologies tend to be amplified by LLMs, consequently constraining model learning and reasoning capabilities. To address this, we propose a novel model named CarbonGPT. This innovative model employs a causal encoder to uncover genuine cross-variable causal relationships, while incorporating a meta causal graph dictionary and lightweight alignment to enhance the comprehension of carbon feature representations by LLMs in EV and RES grid integration scenarios. Extensive simulations in PDNs under large-scale integration of EVs and RESs have demonstrated that CarbonGPT consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance in both prediction accuracy and effectiveness. title: A Distributed Multi-Energy Optimal Coordination Scheme Exploiting Neighborhood Flexibility
abstract: The optimal coordination of distributed energy resources in large residential neighborhoods presents a critical and computationally challenging problem in demand-side management. To fully exploit demand-side flexibility, we propose a decentralized scheme to address this challenge, in which multiple energy sources and social interactions among residents are taken into account. Local operations are cast as mixed-integer subproblems, organized into blocks to integrate social factors, while several linking constraints are enforced at the neighborhood level. Exploiting this structure, we propose to tackle the dual problem in a distributed manner, followed by primal feasibility recovery. The cutting plane algorithm presented is novel in its asynchronous concurrent mechanism, and its efficiency is validated through multiple tests across various problem configurations. In a one-device-per-block setting with 443 households, our algorithm is able to find relative gap < 0.1% solutions in 2 minutes. In a large-scale test with millions of decision variables out of 28336 households, our algorithm managed to find relative gap < 0.01% solutions within 310 seconds. Unlike existing studies using mainly synchronized algorithms in simulations, ours reflects realistic operating conditions better. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness and applicability of the proposed methodology in addressing complex real-world coordination problems.

title: Multi-Frequency Injection Based Wideband Signal Measurement Method and Its Application in Grid-Connected Inverter
abstract: Wideband impedance characteristics play an essential role in renewable energy grid-connected stability analysis, and multi-frequency injection based wideband signal measurement is an effective method to extract impedance characteristics quickly. However, due to the spectral leakage and low frequency resolution, existing measurement methods such as fast Fourier transform (FFT) suffer from poor measurement accuracy under multi-frequency conditions. To tackle this issue, a wideband measurement method is proposed to extract grid-inverter impedance characteristics from the time-domain perspective. First, the concept of deterministic components in impedance measurement is introduced, and the impedance measurement is regarded as deterministic components measurement. Then, a high-precision deterministic components measurement method is proposed. By approximating the fundamental frequency through a first polynomial fitting and then solving the deterministic components through a second polynomial fitting, the deterministic components can be accurately extracted in the presence of fundamental frequency deviation and noise. To validate the performance of the proposed method, simulations and actual measurement experiments are carried out. The results demonstrate that the impedance amplitude errors of the proposed method are less than 1.8 dB, and the phase errors are less than 5.5° under the test conditions, which are significantly lower than those of existing wideband measurement methods.

title: Emergency Computation Offloading for Virtual Power Plants Under Edge Server DDoS Attacks
abstract: Cloud-edge collaboration enables virtual power plants (VPPs) to efficiently manage demand-side resources (DSRs). However, it also exposes VPPs to the threat of edge server distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks, which can undermine the dispatchable power capability of a VPP by exhausting its computational resources. This article formulates an emergency computation offloading model to guide the collaboration between cloud servers and edge servers to maximize the dispatchable power of VPP. The model identifies analytically the range of attack intensities where a VPP can maintain full dispatchable power and where the VPP cannot. It also uncovers the convexity property of VPP’s dispatchable power. The proposed model is submodular so that an efficient submodular optimization algorithm can be developed to alleviate the curse of dimensionality inherent in the computation offloading problem. Numerical studies were carried out on the VPP with 9,951 DSRs to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. A small-scale VPP was also selected to show that the proposed method offers comparable performance, but much less computational cost, to deep reinforcement learning methods.

title: Fractional-Order Distributed Current Sharing Control for Power-Coupled Multi-Bus DC Microgrids: A Hierarchical Consensus Approach
abstract: Although the primary fractional-order PI controller, which can improve dynamic response features, has been widely applied in DC microgrids, the relative distributed secondary control has not been proposed to achieve accurate current sharing for multi-bus DC microgrids with power coupling items and composite load generalized disturbances (including constant power/current loads). Thus, this paper introduces a fractionalorder distributed secondary control (FODSC) strategy specifically designed for such multi-bus DC microgrids. Firstly, the standard fractional-order multi-agent state-space function model is built, including a primary fractional-order PI controller, a power coupling item, and so on. This standard model is an important foundation for hierarchical control design. Secondly, the state compensator is designed to solve the heterogeneous problem, which is caused by different energy resource rated capacity, RLC filter, and so on. Furthermore, the fractional-order distributed secondary control strategy is proposed to achieve accurate current sharing for multi-bus DC microgrids with power coupling items, effectively overcoming the negative damping effect induced by constant power loads. Meanwhile, the stability proof of the proposed control strategy is provided. Furthermore, a cyber-physical resilient mechanism is integrated to enable plug-and-play operations and system fault tolerance. Finally, simulation and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) experimental results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness and practical implementability of the proposed strategy in achieving accurate current sharing.

title: A Structure-Preserved Control Approach for Dynamic Load-Altering Attacks in Power Systems
abstract: Dynamic load-altering attacks (D-LAAs) pose a significant threat to power systems and demand response programs by destabilizing the grid through the manipulation of vulnerable, controllable loads. Despite the development of various detection, protection, and mitigation strategies, the majority of them are based on transforming descriptor-type power systems into ordinary differential equations, which often introduce challenges that limit their effectiveness, particularly under constraint violations. In this paper, we present a novel linear-quadratic regulator (LQR) control method that directly addresses the D-LAA problem, which happens at multiple points, without relying on transformations to any restricted system equivalence. First, we model the under-attack power system as a cyber-physical power system (CPPS) to establish conditions for solvability and admissibility based on the topological structure. Next, we utilize a regularized least-squares framework to generate a quadratic cost function, which we then connect to a constrained recursive minimization problem to develop an LQR algorithm through dynamic programming. To accomplish this, we employ the derived algorithm on CPPS to mitigate D-LAAs and stabilize the system. We validate the proposed approach using the IEEE standard test systems as case studies, demonstrating the feasibility of an effective mitigation strategy against D-LAAs.

title: Learning Active Constraints for Bilevel Optimization: Evaluating Classification Metrics on Real-World Distribution System Data
abstract: Bilevel optimization provides a useful power system modeling framework, but it is computationally demanding due to its NP-hard nature and the need for frequent solutions under uncertainty. To mitigate this, machine learning can be used to predict active constraints, enabling the deduction of a reduced problem formulation. However, prediction errors are inevitable, and synthetic training data may not fully reflect real-world conditions. This paper presents a structured approach to managing uncertainty by classifying constraints into three sets – active, inactive, and unpredictable – where each constraint is modeled using a separate binary classifier. The method is applied to a real-world bilevel distribution system optimization problem: the upper level solves an AC Optimal Power Flow, while the lower level minimizes residential photovoltaic power curtailment. Training data are generated from daily exact bilevel solutions, incorporating variability in electricity prices, consumption, and photovoltaic power generation. Results show that the reduced formulation effectively solves the problem, up to 10 times faster with a marginal objective value deviation (−3% to + 4%).

title: TD3-Enhanced Adaptive Active Disturbance Rejection Control for Bidirectional DC-DC Converter in Photovoltaic-Battery Hybrid Microgrids
abstract: This paper addresses the stability and reliability issues associated with the application of linear active disturbance rejection control (LADRC) in hybrid PV-battery microgrids. A hierarchical control strategy tailored for bidirectional DC-DC converter in the system is proposed. The strategy comprises an outer voltage regulation loop implemented with an enhanced LADRC and an inner current tracking loop driven by a proportional-integral (PI) controller. Specifically, the traditional LADRC is enhanced via an improved linear extended state observer, which achieves separate compensation for low-order and high-order disturbances. Additionally, the observer parameters are optimized in real time based on the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm. Finally, simulations and experiments under multiple operating conditions are conducted to validate the proposed control strategy, demonstrating its superior performance over double closed-loop PI control and traditional LADRC.

title: Detection of Out-of-Distribution Power Quality Disturbance using Dual-Channel Gramian Angular Field with Enhanced Mahalanobis Distance
abstract: Deep learning methods for the power quality disturbance (PQD) classification encounter significant deployment challenges in power system applications. With the increasing integration of renewable energy, electric vehicles, and other non-traditional loads, the out-of-distribution (OOD) data occurs frequently due to evolving power system conditions, which represents a critical yet underexplored challenge. In this study, the OOD problem in the PQD classification is formally defined, where models encounter the absence of disturbance patterns during training. Leveraging the unique characteristics of PQD data, a four-stage multimodal OOD detection method is developed for the OOD-driven framework to enhance PQD classification. The proposed method first transforms PQD waveforms into dual-channel Gramian Angular Field (GAF) maps, then extracts discriminative features with vision Transformers. Mahalanobis distance is employed for OOD scoring, and a multimodal auxiliary criterion is introduced to enhance the distinction between in-distribution (IND) and OOD. Comprehensive case studies are conducted using both simulated IEEE standard-compliant waveforms and practical PQD data. Results applied to the simulated PQD data demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve a 2.10% of false positive rate at 95% true positive recall (FPR95), outperforming all previous methods. Practical applications demonstrate a remarkable 9.64% improvement in the PQD classification accuracy compared to the unfiltered dataset containing OOD samples.

title: Distributed dynamic event-triggered secondary control in dually heterogeneous islanded PV–BESS microgrids for voltage–frequency regulation and SoC balancing
abstract: High penetration of grid-following (GFL) PVs and grid-forming (GFM) storage/hybrid units creates islanded microgrids with dual heterogeneity in composition and control. In such systems, stochastic power injections from GFL units act as fast-varying disturbances to GFM units, which frequently violate fixed thresholds of conventional static event-triggered mechanisms, leading to excessive communication overhead. To address these challenges, this paper develops a fully distributed, dynamic event-triggered secondary control framework for dually heterogeneous microgrids. A unified controller achieves simultaneous frequency/voltage regulation, while ensuring accurate active power sharing and state-of-charge balancing exclusively for battery storage units. Importantly, a fully decentralized, graph-Laplacian-free dynamic triggering mechanism, synergized with local state predictors, is introduced. By employing an internal adaptive variable and relying solely on local states, this mechanism decouples event generation from communication topology, tolerating transient fluctuations without continuous neighbor monitoring. Lyapunov analysis guarantees global stability and excludes Zeno behavior. Hardware-in-the-loop tests validate that the proposed scheme maintains stability under complex dynamics, severe communication delays, and sensor noise, reducing communication traffic by over 90% and 84% compared with periodic and static event-triggered benchmarks, respectively.

title: Co-optimization of Coincident Peak Management and Ancillary Services for Flexible Data Centers
abstract: Flexible Data Centers (FDCs) have become an important demand-side resource in power systems as their scale and flexibility continue to grow. By rescheduling interruptible and delayable computing tasks, FDCs can rapidly adjust power consumption and participate in electricity market activities such as demand response and ancillary services (AS). Meanwhile, many electricity markets adopt a coincident peak (CP) mechanism, under which FDCs may incur substantial charges if they fail to reduce load during peak hours. As a result, FDC operations must balance computing performance, market revenue, and CP risk. Under these conditions, the major challenge is to determine operating strategies that can simultaneously satisfy computing needs, support market participation, and reduce peak-related penalties under uncertain CP events and multiple market objectives. This paper proposes a unified co-optimization methodology for FDC operations. A high-fidelity physical–economic model is first constructed to capture the relationship between input power, computational throughput, and economic returns. Then, a model-agnostic three-stage CP prediction strategy is developed to identify periods with high CP risk. Building on these components, a risk-driven and prediction-aware co-optimization methodology (RPCM) is developed to jointly optimize baseline workloads, AS bids, and peak-avoidance actions. Case studies in the ERCOT market in Texas show that the proposed method achieves significantly higher overall profit than traditional approaches that treat these decisions separately, as it can effectively avoid CP charges while increasing AS revenue. The results demonstrate that the proposed methodology provides a practical and robust decision tool for FDC operators under multi-market conditions.

title: Intelligent Faulted Span Localization for Overhead Power Distribution Networks by Non-Contact Magnetic Sensing
abstract: Power distribution network is a critical link of Power grid throughout the world, where overhead power lines transport electricity from substation to the consumers end. Short circuit faults are common and contribute to more than 50% for the total faults in distribution lines, mainly due to insulation failures, vegetation growth, birding and line intrusion. Such non-clearing faults require manual faulted span retrieval which results in longer outage times and enormous human effort. This work presents and demonstrate a complete system level approach to automates manual fault localization by non-contact magnetic sensing, its processing and rapid reporting of faulted span length. This results in reduced outage time for customers, less patrolling, and improved safety of line personnel. To test and validate, this article further designs a novel Remote Terminal Unit (RTU) to track weak magnetic signatures radiated from overhead lines in a non-contact arrangement to detect and identify distribution line status. The state from deployed RTUs is further transmitted to cloud-based algorithm to identify faulted span length. The RTU is developed to cater for real world modalities such as ease of installation at a distance from live conductors, and ability to withstand geomagnetic, ferromagnetic as well as intrinsic sensor noise. The presented system is implementable to radial as well as meshed based modern power systems with an inbuilt mechanism to prevent false alarm in events of back feeding and inrush current. High voltage lab and extensive on-field testing verifies the overall system efficacy to successfully localize the faulted span length.

title: Dynamic Interactions and Stabilization of Flexible Multi-Terminal Medium-Voltage DC Grid for EV Charging Stations and PV Generation Integration
abstract: Multi-terminal medium-voltage dc (MVDC) grids are emerging as a promising solution for effectively integrating renewable energy resources and supplying the growing demand for dc loads, such as EV charging stations (EVCSs). However, ensuring their stable operation under varying operating conditions remains a significant challenge. This paper addresses the stability and dynamic interactions of a typical MVDC grid integrating EVCSs and PV generation via dual-active-bridge converters, an ac grid via a voltage-source converter (VSC), and a power flow controller (PFC). Using a comprehensive linearized state-space model, eigenvalue and frequency response analyses reveal that the MVDC system stability is jeopardized during the discharging operation of EVCSs, in the presence of the power feedforward compensation loop in the dc voltage controller of the VSC; such stability challenges become more pronounced in weak ac grid connections. A novel active damping controller integrated with the PFC control strategy is proposed to stabilize the MVDC system, extending the PFC capabilities to offer system-level damping in addition to power flow management. Offline and real-time simulation studies confirm the analytical findings and validate the stabilization efficacy of the proposed compensator.

title: Time–Load Joint Optimization for Accelerating Resilient Restoration of Distribution Grids: A Three-Stage Decentralized Human–Robot–Mobile Power Sources Heterogeneous Collaboration Recovery Support System
abstract: Ice storms and rapidly growing EV charging demand create coupled challenges for post-disaster restoration of distribution systems (DSs). Most existing restoration schemes optimize either the time dimension (e.g., crew/task scheduling) or the load dimension (e.g., restored demand) in isolation, while rarely coordinating heterogeneous agents such as de-icing robots (DRs), repair crews (RCs), mobile charging suppliers (MCSs), mobile energy storage systems (MESSs), and mobile emergency generators (MEGs) within one recovery process. To address this gap, this paper proposes a three-stage time–load joint optimization framework that organizes de-icing, repair, EV service, and mobile power support into one coordinated recovery chain. Stage I co-schedules DRs and RCs on a time-expanded network to accelerate structural restoration under safety and energization logic. Stage II dispatches MCS fleets through a tri-objective model that balances supplier operating cost, soft time-window based EV service satisfaction, and voltage-resilience deviation. Stage III coordinates MESSs and MEGs for radial-island restoration of fixed critical loads and residual EV demand. Rather than simply concatenating multiple restoration tasks, the proposed framework explicitly links the three stages through restoration-state transfer. In this way, structural recovery, EV mobile-load restoration, and islanded load pickup are coordinated to jointly improve restoration speed and restored load level in EV-rich disaster-affected DSs.

title: Closed-Loop Probabilistic Forecasting Method of Short-Term Spatial Load Considering Corrupted Data and Field Verification
abstract: The rapid development of flexible load technologies brings new challenges to short-term spatial load forecasting (SSLF) in distribution networks (DNs). Conventionally, as an open-loop method, SSLF is unable to dynamically improve the forecast results. However, the nonstationary and volatility features of loads reduce the accuracy of the SSLF, the errors caused by load data loss and distortion further reduce the robustness of the forecasting. In this paper, we propose a closed-loop probabilistic forecasting method for the SSLF by integrating the modified Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional network (ST-GCN) and the statistical load baseline profile (SLBP). The modified ST-GCN consists of GCN-Gate Recurrent Unit (GCN-GRU) and GCN in parallel to simultaneously learn the spatio-temporal correlation of loads. To capture the uncertainty of the SSLF, the concrete dropout enabled Bayesian neural networks are applied. The SLBP, which is calculated by statistical method, is used to extract the periodicity of the load and mitigate the impact caused by corrupted data. The closed-loop forecasting architecture is devised to integrate the modified ST-GCN and SLBP by the dynamic clustering technique, to in turn improve the accuracy and the robustness of the forecasting results. Numerical tests are conducted using the real load data of DNs in China. Test results confirmed the superiority of the proposed method.

title: Reconnection-Time-Optimal Fractional-Chaotic SIR-Gossip Control for Resilient Microgrid Islanding and Reconnection
abstract: The rapid growth of distributed renewable generation and inverter-based resources has heightened the need for control strategies that guarantee both safety and freshness during microgrid islanding and reconnection, such as those used in real-time dynamic network environments. In the specific scenario of microgrid reconnection, existing schemes like randomized gossip, asynchronous gossip, and fractional-order consensus can not effectively exploit fractional memory and trust-SIR dynamics, leading to slow convergence and high reconnection time. In this paper, we propose a unified fractional-chaotic susceptible-infected-recovered (SIR)-Gossip controller (UFSC) to solve the existing problem of minimizing reconnection time while ensuring safety, integrity, and freshness. By optimizing the closed-form exponents and utilizing a co-designed framework of trust recovery, risk expansion, and consensus acceleration, our approach achieves provably minimal reconnection time and superior consensus accuracy. The experiment results demonstrate the advantages of our approach in improving reconnection time by up to 46% and reducing consensus error by up to 30%, outperforming traditional methods in terms of synchronization, trust recovery, and overall system performance.

title: Physics-Aware Recurrent and Graphical Learning for Robust Distribution System State Estimation Across Unseen Networks
abstract: Robust distribution system state estimation (DSSE) is increasingly vital in modern, complex networks. However, conventional optimization-based DSSE approaches often face challenges with real-time complexity. Consequently, recent advancements have introduced learning-based, physics-aware DSSE methods that leverage network structural information to enhance model effectiveness. Among these methods, graph neural networks (GNNs) have gained prominence as an effective DSSE solution. However, GNN-based models encounter significant challenges in practical DSSE applications, due to their reliance on aggregating and propagating features only from adjacent nodes. To address this limitation, this paper presents a novel physics-aware DSSE framework. It integrates a structure-aware recurrent neural network and GNN with convolutional autoregressive moving average layers for improved feature aggregation and propagation. This model significantly enhances robustness and transferability across diverse unseen network topologies. The scalability of the proposed framework is demonstrated through extensive testing on real distribution systems. The proposed method demonstrates superior performance compared to existing methods by an average of 0.625% MAPE and 0.0093 rad. MAE in normal scenario under unseen networks. Additional ablation and measurement availability studies further verify the robustness and effectiveness of the proposed framework. The framework offers a pragmatic solution for DSSE, ensuring precise state estimation even in challenging environments.

title: Emission and Economy Balanced Dispatching of Integrated Power and Hydrogen Systems via a Tri-Level Robust Optimizer Incorporating Multi-Time Resolution and Carbon Tax
abstract: The escalating demand for hydrogen forces hydrogen generation station (HGS) to seek a stable power supply, that is inherently contradicts the intermittency of distributed renewable energy (DRE). Whilst the affordable active distribution network (ADN) electricity mostly sourced from fossil fuels goes against decarbonization vision. To balance economy and emission, an efficient integrated power and hydrogen system (IPHS), featuring a full-cycle carbon tax and hybrid energy storage, is proposed. Particularly, the full-cycle carbon tax fosters optimized utilization of clean energies and development of high-efficiency solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC). The ADN involves li-ion batteries to derisk DRE curtailment. Whilst a two-layer optimizer is proposed to lower emission of the HGS, where the inner layer leverages a vehicle routing problem (VRP) to decarbonize hydrogen selling, and the outer layer serves to improve efficiency of hydrogen production and conversion. On privacy barrier, the ADN and HGS are unified by alternated directed multiplier method (ADMM), yielding a tri-level robust model. Given the integer-rich NP-hard nature of this model, due to 5-minute battery scheduling and inner VRP, a multi-time resolution solver is tailored. It segregates IPHS operations into a 1-hour ADN-HGS interaction stage following HGS’s slow responses, and an enhanced fast 5-minute battery schedule phase to compensate DRE stochasticity. Numerical studies indicate that, the proposed model reduces carbon emissions by at least 20.5% and operating costs by 7.6% across various seasonal scenarios.

title: Resilience Enhancement of Cyber-Physical Distribution Systems by Coordinating Unmanned Aerial Vehicles and Multi-Function Emergency Trucks
abstract: The post-disaster recovery of cyber-physical distribution systems (CPDS) critically depends on the coordinated restoration of the inter-dependent communication networks (CNs) and power distribution networks (PDNs). The deployment of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) as aerial base stations is a promising strategy for communication restoration, but it is severely hampered by their limited flight endurance. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a comprehensive resilience enhancement framework centered on the synergistic operation of UAVs and multi-function emergency trucks (MFETs). In this paradigm, MFETs not only provide emergency power to the grid but also serve as mobile docking stations for UAV transport, docking, and battery swapping. An extended time-space network model is formulated to characterize the spatio-temporal dynamics and interactions between UAVs and MFETs. In addition, an adaptive UAV working site generation algorithm is developed to optimize UAV placement and scheduling. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is validated using two test systems of different scales. Numerical results demonstrate that the coordinated UAV-MFET operation significantly enhances CPDS resilience. Moreover, the adaptive algorithm improves restoration quality while substantially reducing the computational burden.

title: Virtual Agent and Optimal Communication Network Design for Microgrids Against DoS Attacks
abstract: The implementation of distributed secondary control makes microgrids vulnerable to denial of service (DoS) attacks on communication edges and nodes. To enhance resilience against DoS attacks and increase the survivability of real agents (RAs), this paper proposes a general and practical virtual agent (VA) framework. A lightweight VA update policy is developed and theoretically proven to be non-intrusive to normal system operation, while reducing the success rate of DoS edge and node attacks. Further, a VA-aware communication topology optimization problem is formulated to optimally connect VAs, maximizing RA survivability. Then an efficient algorithm is developed to solve the formulated problem for large-scale systems. A hardware testbed is developed with real communication protocols to replicate practical network conditions. Simulations on a 4-DG microgrid and experiments on the hardware testbed validate that the proposed method preserves normal system operation and significantly enhances resilience under DoS attacks. Additional numerical results on the IEEE 34-bus system further demonstrate the effectiveness of the optimized topology in improving RA survivability.

title: Multi-view Graph Attributed Learning Data Imputation Method for Residential Load Analysis
abstract: With the proliferation of smart grids, residential load data has become vital for user behavior modeling and demand forecasting. However, real-world load curves frequently suffer from substantial missing values due to sensor or communication failures, making accurate imputation crucial. Existing data imputation methods encounter two main challenges. On the one hand, they often suffer significant performance degradation under high missing rates. On the other hand, they lack generalization across users, limiting their ability to accurately impute load curves for households with limited daily load curves. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a multi-view graph-attributed imputation framework. It constructs an observation-aware similarity graph using mask alignment to ensure structural reliability under sparse observations and introduces higher-order temporal gradient features to represent load dynamics. These views are fused through self-expressive learning and graph embedding to reveal latent user structures and guide robust imputation. Experiments on real-world residential data demonstrate the method’s superior performance, particularly under severe missingness and limited target load data.

title: Joint Optimization of Collaborative Routes and Charging Infrastructure for Electric Trucks and Drones in Emergency Logistics
abstract: In sparsely populated and disaster-prone regions, delivering critical resources like medical and emergency supplies presents significant challenges. These scenarios require highly efficient logistics systems, such as integrating Electric Trucks (ETs) and Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) to enhance emergency logistics. This paper proposes a dynamic joint optimization model to address coordinated route planning and dual charging needs for ET and drones, maximizing delivery efficiency while adapting to real-time disruptions. The model minimizes overall investment, construction, and time penalty costs while optimizing service coverage and strategically locating delivery routes and charging stations under battery range constraints. A real case study in the San Francisco area evaluates the model’s performance, comparing it to scenarios without drone charging stations, the proposed model reduces delay costs by 40.07% and improves the on-time delivery rate by 27.26%. Under adverse conditions including wind speed surges, traffic delays, mechanical or communication failures, demand surges, and battery degradation, the proposed model achieves on-time delivery rates ranging from 85.51% to 96.42%, significantly outperforming the baseline’s rates of 25.83% to 75.65%, demonstrating the model’s ability to adapt to dynamic conditions and provide a robust solution for future emergency logistics systems.

title: Incentive Compatible Online Pricing of Customer Directrix Load-Based Demand Response for Load Aggregators
abstract: In demand response (DR) programs, load aggregators (LAs) coordinate DR customers to provide flexibility support for the smart grid. However, existing pricing mechanisms often struggle to simultaneously achieve incentive compatibility and operational controllability in retail-side DR. To address this challenge, this paper proposes an incentive compatible online pricing strategy for customer directrix load (CDL)-based DR of LAs. Unlike traditional price-based DR schemes, the proposed approach leverages CDL, which inherently enhances controllability by serving as both the guiding signal and the performance evaluation metric. Within the CDL framework, a DR customer response model and an LA centralized optimization model are established. Under a general discomfort function setting, the centralized response is characterized by a one-dimensional fixed-point equation, based on which a customized incentive compatible pricing strategy is derived to align individual customer responses with the LA’s desired response curve. Furthermore, the widely used quadratic discomfort model is studied as an analytically tractable special case, leading to closed-form response and pricing expressions. An online learning algorithm is then proposed to enable LAs to learn the unobservable discomfort parameters of DR customers from observable response decisions, thereby reducing information exposure and enhancing practical implementation performance. The proposed algorithm is theoretically shown to achieve logarithmic regret with respect to the operating cycle, and a problem-level regret lower bound is further established to show that the minimax cumulative regret of the underlying CDL-based online pricing problem is also logarithmic. Simulation results based on real-world data demonstrate the validity and effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Optimal Placement of Smart Hybrid Transformers in Distribution Networks
abstract: Hybrid transformers are a relatively new technology that combine conventional power transformers with power electronics to provide voltage and reactive power control capabilities in distribution networks. This paper proposes a novel method of determining the optimal location and utilisation of hybrid transformers in 3-phase distribution networks to maximise the net present value of hybrid transformers based on their ability to increase the export of power produced by distributed generators over their operational lifespan. This has been accomplished through sequential linear programming, a key feature of which is the consideration of nonlinear characteristics and constraints relating to hybrid transformer power electronics and control capabilities. Test cases were carried out in a modified version of the Cigre European Low Voltage Distribution Network Benchmark, which has been extended by connecting it with two additional low voltage distribution test networks. All test case results demonstrate that the installation and utilisation of hybrid transformers can improve the income earned from exporting excess active power, justifying their installation cost (with the highest net present value being (6.56 million, resulting from a 45.53% increase in estimated annual profits due to coordinated HT compensation).

title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Multi-UAV Deployment for Power Corridor Monitoring With Satellite Internet
abstract: Uncrewed Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-assisted communication offers a solution for monitoring remote power corridors, but existing methods struggle to balance heterogeneous monitoring demands and UAV resource constraints, limiting efficiency in large-scale operations. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a reinforcement learning-based multi-UAV deployment for power corridor monitoring with satellite internet. First, an integrated UAV-satellite monitoring framework is developed to enhance communication stability, ensuring seamless data transmission and continuous monitoring in large-scale scenarios. Second, a risk-aware monitoring demand quantification model is introduced to handle spatially heterogeneous risks by using a data-driven risk-weighted prioritization mechanism to dynamically allocate sensor resources under multi-risk conditions. Third, a contextual Multi-Armed Bandit (MAB)-based UAV deployment algorithm is proposed to balance energy efficiency and data collection performance, ensuring sustainable UAV operations and Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI)-compatible monitoring. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior energy efficiency, data collection performance, and convergence speed compared to existing methods, validating its feasibility for large-scale UAV-based power corridor monitoring and AMI-enabled grid intelligence.

title: QUPID: A Partitioned Quantum Neural Network for Anomaly Detection in Smart Grid
abstract: Smart grid infrastructures have revolutionized energy distribution, but their day-to-day operations require robust anomaly detection methods to counter risks associated with cyber-physical threats and system faults potentially caused by natural disasters, equipment malfunctions, and cyber attacks. Conventional machine learning (ML) models are effective in several domains, yet they struggle to represent the complexities observed in smart grid systems. Furthermore, traditional ML models are highly susceptible to adversarial manipulations, making them increasingly unreliable for real-world deployment. Quantum ML (QML) provides a unique advantage, utilizing quantum-enhanced feature representations to model the intricacies of the high-dimensional nature of smart grid systems while demonstrating greater resilience to adversarial manipulation. In this work, we propose QUPID, a partitioned quantum neural network (PQNN) that outperforms traditional state-of-the-art ML models in anomaly detection. We extend our model to R-QUPID that even maintains its performance when including differential privacy (DP) for enhanced robustness. Moreover, our partitioning framework addresses a significant scalability problem in QML by efficiently distributing computational workloads, making quantum-enhanced anomaly detection practical in large-scale smart grid environments. Our experimental results in various scenarios exemplify the efficacy of QUPID and R-QUPID to significantly improve anomaly detection capabilities and robustness compared to traditional ML approaches.

title: Market-Driven Joint Trading Strategy for Computing Service and Electricity in Cloud-Edge Collaborative Systems
abstract: The rapid growth of cloud-edge collaborative computing and its increasing electricity demand are forging strong interdependencies between computing and power markets. This paper proposes a market-driven joint trading strategy that coordinates computing services and electricity procurement within a cloud-edge collaborative system. To capture heterogeneous operational characteristics, we introduce a differentiated modeling paradigm, combining a task-queuing model for the cloud data center with an empirically-grounded nonlinear delay model for edge servers to characterize its performance saturation. These models are then embedded in a unified trading framework that explicitly characterizes the bidirectional interaction between computing and electricity markets, where the cloud acts as a price-making participant. The resulting large-scale, non-convex problem is transformed into a tractable mixed-integer second-order cone program by applying targeted convexification techniques—specifically, second-order cone relaxation for nonlinear delay constraints and special ordered sets of type 2 for bilinear market-clearing terms. Numerical case studies demonstrate that the differentiated modeling paradigm reduces the overall operational cost of the test system by 16.3%, including both electricity and delay costs. Furthermore, the solution methodology ensures high scalability and computational efficiency for large-scale instances while maintaining an optimality gap below 0.3%.

title: Reputation Attack Detection-Based Resilient Distributed Energy Management of Cyber-Physical Microgrid
abstract: Due to potential cyber attack, it brings a great challenge for energy management of micro-grid. To address these problems, a reputation-detection-based resilient distributed energy management approach is proposed. To well detect false data injection (FDI) and denial of service (DoS) attacks, this paper presents a reputation mechanism to detect the potential cyber attack combined with acknowledgment (ACK) signal by evaluation index from its neighbor nodes. Those identified adversarial nodes can be compensated with coordinated information from high-reputation nodes. To fight against those cyber attacks, a resilient distributed optimization approach is proposed with event-triggered mechanism, which corrects those adversarial nodes with a compensation mechanism, which can ensure the convergence even under both FDI and DoS attack. According to those simulation results, it reveals that the proposed approach can converge well under both FDI and DoS attack, which can provide a promising viable approach for security-based energy management of cyber-physical micro-grid.

title: A Physics-Guided Deep Learning Framework for Wide-Band Oscillation Parameter Estimation in Power Systems
abstract: This paper introduces a physics-guided deep learning model for wide-band oscillations (WBO) parameters estimation. The model first utilizes the damped oscillation model to generate synthetic datasets covering low-frequency, sub-/super-synchronous, and mid-to-high frequency oscillations. Then, a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) is used to produce noise-augmented datasets that reflect real-world conditions, overcoming the challenge of insufficient WBO samples for deep learning training. Further, a long short-term memory (LSTM) network is exploited to extract temporal features from WBO signals and identify parameters, including amplitude, damping factor, frequency, and phase. Experimental results show that the LSTM-cGAN model outperforms other state-of-the-art deep learning methods in parameter estimation in accuracy. Moreover, the effectiveness of the approach is validated using both PSCAD/EMTDC-simulated oscillation data and real-world oscillation measurements.

title: Optimal Planning of Voltage-Regulating Active Power Filters for Meshed Cable Distribution Networks Considering Harmonic Propagation Paths
abstract: With the widespread application of cable lines in urban distribution grids, the amplification of harmonic standing waves has become increasingly prominent, leading to significant power quality deterioration. To mitigate this issue, this paper proposes an optimal planning strategy for voltage-regulating active power filters (VRAPFs) in meshed cable distribution grids, explicitly accounting for harmonic propagation paths. First, a harmonic propagation model is established to characterize typical scenarios with varying propagation characteristics. Subsequently, K-means clustering is applied to the propagation coefficients, partitioning the distribution grid into regions where nodes exhibit similar harmonic behaviors. Within each region, the node with the highest propagation coefficient is selected as the installation site of the VRAPF to ensure uniform harmonic suppression. Furthermore, the operational parameters of the VRAPF are optimized to simultaneously satisfy network performance requirements and minimize total cost. Comparative analyses with alternative site-selection strategies validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed approach.

title: Aggregate Grid-Forming Control of Distributed Energy Resources
abstract: This article presents an aggregate grid-forming control for heterogeneous distributed energy resources (DERs). The proposed control achieves a desired, aggregated grid-forming response by coordinating power contributions among multiple different DERs. Unlike existing aggregate control strategies that are typically objective-specific or topology-specific, this article proposes a generic, flexible, and modular control design. The design supports four basic module types, i.e., AC- or DC-coupling and AC- or DC-output topological arrangements, adequately accommodating diverse DER integration scenarios, e.g., AC, DC, AC/DC hybrid microgrids, hybrid energy storage systems, or hybrid renewable power plants. The grid-forming control design is systematically developed by aggregating DER dynamics and disaggregating control objectives for the four basic modules, then extended to modular configurations through a top-down approach. The grid-forming performance is comprehensively validated through simulation and experiments. This modular control design provides scalable and standardizable grid interfaces, enabling effective aggregation of heterogeneous DERs to jointly achieve grid-forming dynamic response.

title: Data-Driven Distribution Network Modeling Using Shallow Physics-Informed Neural Network
abstract: Accurate topology and line parameters are fundamental for the planning, operation, and control of distribution networks. Motivated by the physics and characteristics of the distribution network power flow, a shallow physics-informed neural network (SPINN), based on the input convex neural network (ICNN), is elegantly designed to perform data-driven distribution network modeling, enabling the joint estimation of distribution network topology and line parameters. The proposed data-driven distribution network modeling establishes an analytical expression and mapping between the SPINN parameters and distribution network parameters, allowing the distribution network parameters, i.e., topologies and line parameters, to be directly calculated and inferred from the neural network parameters. The performance of the distribution network modeling method is further proved theoretically and verified on the IEEE 33, 69, and 123-bus systems. The results show that our proposed method can accurately estimate the topology and line parameters.

title: Grid-Interactive and Dual-Side Demand Responsive Timetable Scheduling Optimization for Flexible Urban Metro Systems
abstract: Metro systems, as major electricity consumers, establish a critical demand-side linkage between public transportation services and the utility power grid. With ongoing expansion, metro systems impose increasing challenges on electricity supply due to their concentrated energy demands, while also offering significant potential as controllable loads to enhance grid flexibility. To enhance grid flexibility while effectively meeting passenger demand, this paper proposes a novel dual-side demand-responsive and grid-interactive metro operation framework. This framework allows metro systems to support grid-side demand response by aligning operational schedules with grid conditions and passenger demand, without compromising service quality. A spatiotemporal model is established to estimate metro train power consumption under various speed profiles and real-time passenger loads. An adaptive iterative greedy algorithm is developed to coordinate metro operations in response to real-time power system conditions. Unlike global optimization approaches that suffer from exponential complexity, this algorithm employs a sequential and simulation-based decision process. It prioritizes real-time feasibility by making locally optimal dispatching decisions, thereby achieving a practical trade-off between solution optimality and computational speed. The algorithm offers high computational efficiency and dynamically optimizes train timetables and operational modes, thereby improving grid flexibility. Case studies using real-world metro data demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a 17.8% reduction in electricity costs and provides up to 6.56 MW of DR capacity without compromising passenger service. This study reveals the potential of metro systems as large-scale, dispatchable loads that contribute to the flexibility of utility grids.

title: Convex-Hull of Locational Marginal Carbon Emission for Carbon Management Considering Emissions during Non-Steady-State Operation Hours
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy, while essential for decarbonization, can intensify thermal-unit cycling and ramping, aggravate network congestion, and increase emissions during non-steady-state operating periods (i.e., start-ups, shutdowns, and fast ramping). Research indicates that carbon emissions during such hours could increase to 2–6 times those of steady-state operation hours. However, conventional studies often ignore the impact of intertemporal constraints on carbon measurements, leading to significant underestimation of carbon emission. To address this gap, this paper extends the locational marginal carbon emission (LMCE) framework by incorporating non-steady-state hours emissions through a convex-hull-based variant of LMCE (i.e., LMCE2) model. This approach clarifies the endogenous link between nodal prices and carbon intensity and ensures theoretical consistency between electricity pricing and carbon emission calculation. The LMCE2 can be efficiently computed using the Dantzig–Wolfe decomposition. We further derive LACE2 that mitigates carbon over-allocation. Our case studies demonstrate that rapid emission assessment during non-steady-state operation hours using LMCE2/LACE2, enables more trustworthy carbon accounting. Compared with traditional LMCE/LACE, the use of LMCE2/LACE2 reduces carbon measurement error by 83.5%–90.1%. The proposed framework offers practical tools for carbon management in electricity markets with high renewable shares.

title: Privacy-preserving Decision-focused Learning for Multi-energy Systems
abstract: Decision-making for multi-energy system (MES) dispatch depends on accurate load forecasting. Traditionally, load forecasting and decision-making for MES are implemented separately. Forecasting models are typically trained to minimize forecasting errors, overlooking their impact on downstream decision-making. To address this, decision-focused learning (DFL) has been studied to minimize decision-making costs instead. However, practical adoption of DFL in MES faces significant challenges: the process requires sharing sensitive load data and model parameters across multiple sectors, raising serious privacy issues. To this end, we propose a privacy-preserving DFL framework tailored for MES. Our approach introduces information masking to safeguard private data while enabling recovery of decision variables and gradients required for model training. To further enhance security for DFL, we design a safety protocol combining matrix decomposition and homomorphic encryption, effectively preventing collusion and unauthorized data access. Additionally, we develop a privacy-preserving load pattern recognition algorithm, enabling the training of specialized DFL models for heterogeneous load patterns. Theoretical analysis and case studies, including real-world MES data, demonstrate that our framework not only protects privacy but also consistently achieves lower average daily dispatch costs compared to existing methods.

title: Co-Optimization of Resource Allocation and Operation in Large-Scale Energy Systems: Part I—Parallel-Distributed Theory
abstract: Integrated resource allocation across heterogeneous operators is imperative to achieve globally optimal planning in large-scale energy systems, yet faces fundamental barriers of computational intractability and stringent privacy protection requirements prohibiting sensitive data sharing. This paper develops a parallel-distributed framework resolving these dual challenges in large-scale planning-operation problems. Particularly, this complex problem is decomposed into two aspects: capacity optimization and location optimization. For the former, an enhanced equivalent projection (EP) technique handling mixed-integer optimization is employed, which compresses operator data into non-reconstructable proxies, reducing variables and ensuring privacy-essential security. For the latter, the location optimization leverages a tree-parallel Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) algorithm that breaks commercial solvers’ resource utilization bottlenecks through asynchronous distributed computing, enabling previously intractable large-scale planning solutions. These innovations unify within a parallel-distributed framework where hierarchical planning center and operators coordination enables simultaneous privacy preservation through encrypted EP exchanges and computational acceleration via parallel MCTS processing. An illustrative example is presented at the end of this paper. In Part II, we deploy this methodology across integrated electricity-gas-heat systems and transmission-distribution networks, and verify its effectiveness in large-scale system planning.

title: A Gaussian Belief Propagation-based Cyber-attack Detection Approach for State Estimation Model in Unbalanced Distribution Networks
abstract: Belief propagation (BP)-based algorithms, typified by their efficient probabilistic inference abilities, are widely used for distributed reasoning in complex systems. However, BP has seldom been studied by the existing literature on unbalanced power distribution networks (PDNs), where state estimation (SE) is faced with exacerbated cybersecurity threats posed by malicious adversaries. To this end, the Gaussian BP (GaBP) with superior efficiency and interpretability is employed in this paper, making it the first attempt to propose a GaBP-based detection approach for unbalanced PDNs against various cyber-attacks. In the proposed approach, the nonlinear SE model is emulated by factor graphs and iteratively solved by GaBP, which is further enhanced using message and factor damping techniques to improve algorithm convergence. By analyzing the belief update procedure in a local factor graph, the measurement update term (MUT) corresponding to the local measurement data is designated as the preliminary attack detection variable. To make the attack-induced temporal shape distortion more perceptible, the proposed approach defines the multivariate derivative dynamic time warping (DDTW) distance between the baseline MUT and the latest MUT sequences as the test statistic. Finally, a generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT) is accordingly designed to detect potential cyber-attacks. Extensive case studies on two modified IEEE test feeders validate the efficacy and superiority of the proposed detection approach.

title: Privacy-Preserving Electricity Theft Detection Training Model Based on Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: In smart grids, electricity theft detection is crucial for ensuring fair billing and reducing utility losses. Most current methods rely on detailed consumption data, posing significant privacy risks. Some privacy-focused detection schemes sacrifice accuracy and ignore protection of model parameters. To overcome these limitations, we propose a privacy-preserving detection framework based on a dual-cloud architecture. Our scheme innovatively combines masking matrix and Boneh–Goh–Nissim (BGN) encryption to establish dual-layer privacy protection: securing user data at the consumption level and preserving training parameter confidentiality throughout the model’s lifecycle. In addition, a self-organizing map (SOM)-convolutional neural network (CNN) is trained to enhance theft detection accuracy under imbalanced data conditions. The experimental results demonstrate that our scheme achieves high detection accuracy with low communication and computation overhead, confirming its practicality and effectiveness.
