title: Enhancing Resilience of Power Distribution Systems Under Cyber-Physical Hybrid Attacks: A Coordinated Localization and Restoration Strategy with Feeder Automation
abstract: The widespread deployment of distributed feeder automation (DFA) has increased the vulnerability of power distribution systems to cyber-physical hybrid attacks. To enhance the resilience of power distribution systems under hybrid attacks, this paper proposes a two-stage integrated cyber-physical system (TICPS) recovery strategy. This strategy integrates hybrid attack localization and isolation, and cyber-physical collaborative restoration, while effectively coordinating multiple resources. In the first stage, a hybrid attack localization module is developed, incorporating an attack descriptive model and a network equivalent transformation method to accurately locate cyber and physical attacks. The localization results are then used to guide DFA to isolate attacked agents and line faults resulting from the attacks. In the second stage, a grid reconfiguration and island formation module is first proposed to achieve efficient load restoration while considering the operational constraints of DFA under a compromised cyber layer. Subsequently, a repair crew dispatch module is designed to optimize crew routing based on value functions of cyber-physical faulty components, thereby facilitating complete cyber-physical system recovery. To leverage sequentially restored and controllable resources during the repair process, a repair event-triggered mechanism is introduced to coordinate grid reconfiguration and crew dispatch. The effectiveness and scalability of the proposed strategy are validated through simulations on the IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 123-bus systems, which demonstrate promising results.

title: Grid Edge Intelligence-Assisted Model Predictive Framework for Black Start of Distribution Systems With Inverter-Based Resources
abstract: The growing proliferation of distributed energy resources (DERs) is significantly enhancing the resilience and reliability of distribution systems. However, a substantial portion of behind-the-meter (BTM) DERs is often overlooked during black start (BS) and restoration processes. Existing BS strategies that utilize grid-forming (GFM) battery energy storage systems (BESS) frequently ignore critical frequency security and synchronization constraints. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a predictive framework for bottom-up BS that leverages the flexibility of BTM DERs through Grid Edge Intelligence (GEI). A predictive model is developed for GEI to estimate multi-period flexibility ranges and track dispatch signals from the utility. A frequency-constrained BS strategy is then introduced, explicitly incorporating constraints on frequency nadir, rate-of-change-of-frequency (RoCoF), and quasi-steady-state (QSS) frequency. The framework also includes synchronizing switches to enable faster and more secure load restoration. Notably, it requires GEI devices to communicate only their flexibility ranges and the utility to send dispatch signals—without exchanging detailed asset information. The proposed framework is validated using a modified IEEE 123-bus test system, and the impact of GEI is demonstrated by comparing results across various GEI penetration scenarios.

title: Resilience-Oriented DG Siting and Sizing Considering Energy Vulnerability Constraint
abstract: Low-income customers are more vulnerable to power outages because they live in areas with poorly equipped distribution systems. However, existing approaches to improve grid resilience focus on the overall system condition and ignore the outage experiences of low-income customers, which leads to significant energy inequities in resilience. Therefore, this paper explores a new resilience-oriented planning method for distributed generator (DG) siting and sizing, by embedding an additional energy vulnerability constraint (EVC). First, the expected load shedding index (ELSI) is defined as the ratio of the load shedding to the original load, which quantifies the resilience-oriented energy vulnerability. Then, the DG siting and sizing problem is formulated as a two-stage stochastic programming with the EVC. The first stage determines the optimal sites and sizes of DG units under investment constraints and EVCs, while the second stage optimizes expected costs of unserved load. A violation variable is introduced to ensure the model’s solvability. Finally, numerical studies are performed on the IEEE 33-bus and 123-bus systems to verify the effectiveness of the proposed DG planning model in reducing energy vulnerability. Three observations are presented as future guidelines for resilience-oriented DG planning.

title: Novel Decentralized Load Shedding Algorithm for Preserving Voltage Stability in Smart Grids
abstract: The occurrence of a short-circuit fault leads to the voltage reduction in power networks, and subsequently, induction motors experience relative speed decrease. This speed decline can sometimes lead to motor stalling for which, motors demand several times their rated current, drawing considerable reactive current. In the networks with a high penetration of motor loads, this can delay voltage recovery, posing a risk of short-term voltage instability. In order to enhance stability, this paper proposes a load shedding index based on kinetic energy to determine the level of kinetic energy of each motor. Motor loads, proportional to their kinetic energy, impose stress on the network. Thus, a load shedding scheme based on this index is presented. Initially, the proposed index is evaluated experimentally for an industrial induction motor and then is assessed on two active distribution networks. Subsequently, to evaluate the comprehensiveness of the index for larger networks, proper appraisal is conducted on a real sizable, multi-voltage-level power grid model and compared to other load-shedding schemes. Results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in addressing short-term voltage instability, requiring less load shedding compared to other approaches. Furthermore, the proposed method is computationally efficient and suitable for real-time implementation.

title: Communication-Constrained Remote Power Grid Resilience Enhancement: Coordinated Planning of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles and Mobile Energy Storage Vehicles
abstract: The underdeveloped power and communication infrastructures in remote areas are prone to simultaneous failure during extreme disasters, exacerbating the difficulty of power system recovery. Mobile energy storage vehicles (MESVs) and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) can achieve the coordination of power and communication, providing precise and effective power support for remote power grid. However, the coordinated planning of MESVs and UAVs is constrainted by factors such as endurance, coverage, and connection. The relationship between these constraints and the performance of dispatching flexibility and resilience support has not been well investigated. This paper proposes a deployment-dispatching two-stage coordinated planning framework of UAVs and MESVs to enhance the remote power grid resilience. The topology-based UAV deployment model and the power flow based MESV deployment mode is proposed. The coordinated dispatching model for UAVs and MESVs considering communication availability is proposed. The test case on IEEE 33 node system and application case on a remote power grid in Northwest China is conducted. The results show that the spatial dispatching flexibility in exchange for communication and traffic constraints significantly improves the resilience support performance of MESVs.

title: A Unified Virtual Battery Modeling Framework for Flexibility Characterization of Building HVAC Systems
abstract: The heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems dominate building’s energy consumption and meanwhile exhibit substantial operational flexibility that can be exploited for providing grid services. However, this goal is largely hindered by the difficulty to characterize the system’s operating flexibility due to the complex building thermal dynamics, physical operating limits and human comfort constraints. To address this challenge, this paper develops a unified virtual battery (VB) modeling framework for characterizing the operating flexibility of both single-zone and multi-zone building HVAC systems, enabling responsive buildings to function like virtual batteries. Specifically, a physically meaningful representation state is first identified to represent building thermal conditions under thermal comfort constraints and then a VB model is established for characterizing the operating flexibility of single-zone HVAC systems. We subsequently extend the VB modeling framework to multi-zone HVAC systems and establish zone VB models to characterize the heterogeneous zonal operating flexibility. We further develop a systematic method to aggregate the zone VB models into a unified VB model. The proposed VB model enables a low-order storage-like representation of the operational flexibility of both single-zone and multi-zone buildings. Case studies demonstrate that the VB model can well capture the building thermal dynamics under varying HVAC control policies. In addition, the VB model is validated through demand response (DR) of buildings. The optimal DR strategies can be obtained from the low-order and low-complexity VB model, and the building’s committed DR can be efficiently decomposed to zone-level control inputs while maintaining human thermal comfort.

title: IDAT: An Impact-Driven Adaptive Threshold for Detecting False Data Injection Attacks on Wind Turbines
abstract: The increasing deployment of wind power systems has raised concerns about their vulnerability to cyberattacks due to remote locations and insecure communication protocols. False data injection (FDI) attacks can bypass detection mechanisms and manipulate system parameters, which may lead to inefficient operation or even failure of wind turbines. In the face of FDI attacks, the first step is to achieve attack detection. However, the strong nonlinearity of wind power systems leads to a difficult problem in detection threshold selection. To this end, this paper proposes a novel impact-driven adaptive threshold (IDAT) selection methodology to detect FDI attacks on variable-speed wind turbines. Firstly, quantitative and qualitative conclusions are obtained based on in-depth analysis of attack impacts. Then, the framework of a general observer-based detector is analyzed, and the difficulties that may arise during threshold selection are explained. Finally, the completeness condition of the detection mechanism is established, and the threshold is adaptively determined in accordance with the specific impact of each attack, ensuring high interpretability. Extensive simulations are conducted on a 5 MW doubly-fed induction generator-based wind turbine to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: B-DRNet: A Stereo Vision-Based Framework for Safety Distance Monitoring in Substations
abstract: Monitoring the safety distance between maintenance personnel and live components is crucial for ensuring the safe and stable operation of the intelligent power grid. To address this issue, this study proposes a distance measurement framework, B-DRNet, which integrates keypoint detection with binocular stereo perception. The method constructs an innovative detector architecture incorporating three improvements: hierarchical feature aggregation block (HFAB), multi-scale attention hypergraph (MSAH), and a decoupled detection head (DDH), which significantly enhance feature representation capability and improve the detection accuracy of small objects. Meanwhile, a stereo perception module based on GwcNet is employed to obtain dense depth information, and coordinate mapping is utilized to achieve three-dimensional distance measurement. Experimental validation demonstrates that the proposed detector outperforms existing models in both detection performance and operational efficiency, with AP improved by 6.68%, frame rate reaching 333 f/s, and parameter size reduced to 1.05 M. The average distance measurement error is 3.18%, which meets practical application requirements and fully verifies its practicality and reliability in substation safety monitoring. B-DRNet achieves a favorable balance among detection accuracy, operational efficiency, and ranging reliability, enabling stable and accurate three-dimensional safety-distance monitoring in complex substation scenarios and providing an efficient solution for automated safety monitoring in substations.

title: Optimal Harmonic Control Strategy for Distribution Networks Considering the Actual Operating Characteristics of Voltage-Regulating Active Power Filter
abstract: An integrated harmonic optimization strategy for distribution networks typically models control devices as ideal current sources, formulating a convex optimization problem with multiple constraints. However, due to inherent nonlinearities, these devices often exhibit frequency coupling effects, leading to non-ideal harmonic control behavior. This article proposes a harmonic optimal control strategy for distribution networks that accounts for the actual operating characteristics of voltage-regulating active power filters (VRAPFs). First, a complete harmonic state-space (HSS) model of the VRAPF is developed to quantitatively analyze the internal signal exchange process between internal modules of VRAPF, thereby elucidating the mechanism behind frequency coupling effects. Second, a coupled virtual admittance model of the VRAPF is established to reshape the network impedance for improved harmonic suppression. Third, a multi-timescale harmonic control strategy based on coordinated global-local operation is proposed, enabling effective mitigation of harmonic injection uncertainties and ensuring that the harmonic voltage distortion at all distribution-network nodes remains below 4%. The proposed approach is validated through hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) experiments, demonstrating its effectiveness and practicality.

title: Thermal-Mechanical Unified Inertia Estimation and Enhancement of Free Piston Stirling Generator in Island Microgrid
abstract: Compared with power electronic converter and diesel generator, the free piston Stirling generator (FPSG) with maintenance-free features has many advantages such as large overcurrent capability, high reliability, and wide heat source adaptability, as well as providing voltage and frequency references. Therefore, FPSG is a powerful competitor in supplying power to island microgrids and providing inertia to resist disturbance. However, unlike rotating devices, FPSG is a thermal-mechanical coupled system, and the two sets of vibrating components are subjected to approximate sinusoidal harmonic vibration, which poses difficulties for inertia analysis. To fill this gap, this paper provides a method for accurately calculating the frequency and power response during the dynamic process, which is the core of inertia analysis. Subsequently, a unified thermal-mechanical inertia estimation method that considers both the frequency reduction to provide mechanical power and the displacement of pistons increase to convert more thermal power is proposed. Then, the inertia enhancement method is provided, which effectively increases the frequency nadir and transition time. Finally, the proposed inertia estimation and enhancement method is verified through simulation and experiment.

title: Bayesian-Optimized Deep Learning for Adaptive Real-Time FDIA Detection in Smart Grid Demand Response Systems
abstract: Smart grid demand response (DR) systems face escalating threats from False Data Injection Attacks (FDIAs), which corrupt load forecasts to distort real-time pricing, destabilize supply– demand equilibrium, and precipitate cascading grid failures. These intrusions manifest as multi-scale temporal anomalies from transient spikes to prolonged distortions in severely imbalanced datasets. We propose an adaptive deep learning architecture integrating: (i) a variance-adaptive 1D convolutional neural network (CNN) with dynamic kernel scaling to magnify anomalies while attenuating noise; (ii) a temporal-attention bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) to resolve forward–backward dependencies; and (iii) Bayesian optimization (BO) with Matérn kernels to jointly optimize accuracy–latency trade-offs under strict computational constraints. An Enhanced SMOTE-RUS scheme synthesizes minority-class attacks while preserving appliance-level periodicity. Evaluated on 377k half-hourly forecasts from 290 U.S. households, the framework attains 99.26% accuracy, 93.16% F1-score, and 1.2 ms per-sample inference, exceeding the strongest baseline by 21.4%.

title: Calculation of Harmonic-constrained Low Voltage Dynamic Operating Envelopes
abstract: Dynamic operating envelopes (DOEs) establish the feasible range of import and export values for prosumers, moving away from static limits and thereby making it possible to free up more network capacity. With the growing penetration of distributed energy resources (DERs) in low-voltage (LV) distribution networks, methods to quantify DOEs are becoming increasingly important. DERs are also sources of harmonics that until now have been neglected in studies on DOE quantification. We present a non-linear, three-phase harmonic optimal power flow model defined in the current-voltage variable space. The model calculates both export and import DOEs in a real-world LV feeder and representative 906-node LV network. We also examine the impact of non-static DER power factors, the use of root-mean-square (rms) voltage limits in the optimization, and the role of considering harmonic injections. Results illustrate scalability of the developed model and show that considering harmonics reduces DOE export values. The decrease does not occur only because of reaching the total harmonic distortion (THD) limit but also because of a more appropriate representation of rms voltage and current values. Conversely, DOE import values increase under the detailed harmonic model, highlighting potential for higher network imports.These findings provide practical insights for system operators. Incorporating harmonicaware DOEs can improve near real-time network utilization and enable effective management and optimization of active endusers’ DER portfolios.

title: Fully Distributed Fault-Tolerant Secondary Control for Islanded Microgrids with Actuator Faults and Disturbances
abstract: This paper investigates the secondary control problem of AC islanded microgrids (MG) with unknown external disturbances and actuator faults. A fully distributed fault-tolerant secondary control strategy based on adaptive dynamic event-triggered mechanism (DETM) is proposed to address voltage and frequency deviations caused by droop control, achieving active power sharing while effectively reducing the communication burden. Considering the possibility of actuator faults, adaptive laws are introduced to estimate and compensate for fault parameters, thereby improving the system’s fault tolerance. The designed adaptive law and event-triggered mechanism (ETM) are implemented based on a fully distributed framework and do not rely on any global information. Compared with existing work, this paper introduces time-varying auxiliary functions and trigger functions, and obtains a strictly positive minimum trigger interval (MTI) without using global information, thus completely avoiding Zeno behavior in the presence of disturbances, which is more rigorous than simply theoretically excluding Zeno behavior. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy by simulation examples.

title: Privacy-Preserving Residential Short-Term Load Forecasting With Missing Data Tolerance
abstract: Traditional data-driven residential short-term load forecasting methods are faced with two major challenges, i.e., preserving data privacy and addressing missing data. Regarding privacy-preserving, a new two-stage pre-training personalized federated learning framework is proposed to train customized forecasting models with high forecasting accuracy for all households without violating their data privacy. As for the missing data problem, an advanced semi-supervised graph diffusion network model is proposed to address missing “features” and “labels” problems, where “features” and “labels” refer to the required input data of the forecasting model and actual load data of the forecasting day, respectively. Mathematically, a graph feature diffusion mechanism-based feature input and imputation module is developed to mitigate the deficiency imposed by missing “features”. Next, a graph convolutional network-based semi-supervised feature augmented and update module is established to mitigate the negative effects of missing “labels”. An actual power system in China is employed to demonstrate the proposed method, and simulation results indicate that high forecasting accuracy and strong robustness under missing data scenarios are achieved.

title: Incentive Communication Enabled Holonic Framework for Urban-Wide P2P Energy Trading
abstract: Peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading has been recognized as a paradigm that can effectively promote energy sharing among end energy entities, foster local energy economy in urban systems, and maximize the value of distributed renewable energy assets. The current P2P energy trading solutions have performance limitations in supporting trading among large-scale prosumers. This paper proposes a new P2P energy trading system that features a multi-layer holonic structure. Based on the real-time operational condition, the system dynamically forms prosumer coalitions at different scales in a bottom-up manner, supporting on-demand P2P energy trading among prosumers in different geographical locations in an urban system. A multi-level coalition formation scheme and a peer-matching scheme are proposed to facilitate this process, and an incentive communication-enabled deep reinforcement learning-based approach is developed to enable individual prosumers to make energy trading decisions that account for multifaceted influencing factors. Besides, a power flow-aware energy trading adjustment scheme is integrated to ensure the settlement feasibility of the energy trading transactions. Numerical simulations are conducted on an IEEE benchmark system and real-world datasets to validate the proposed system.

title: A Single-Ended Whole-Line Protection for Active Distribution Networks Using Constructed Resonant Boundary Element
abstract: Active distribution networks (ADNs) exhibit characteristics such as topological flexibility and bidirectional power flow, which distinguish them from traditional distribution networks (DNs). These intrinsic characteristics present significant challenges to traditional single-ended protection schemes deployed in conventional DNs. Boundary protection, which is based on the coordination between the relay on one side of the line and the boundary element at the opposite terminal, can achieve rapid fault detection across the entire line utilizing exclusively local information, thereby offering a promising solution for addressing the protection challenges in ADNs. In this paper, a method for constructing a resonant-type boundary element (RBE) is proposed, based on the analysis of the performance of various boundary element types. Furthermore, the fault characteristics for internal and external faults are analyzed. Within the specified blocking frequency band (BFB) of the RBE, the voltage during an internal fault exhibits significantly higher magnitudes compared to those during external faults. Based on this distinction, a voltage energy criterion incorporating fault phase angle correction is subsequently proposed. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed protection method, in conjunction with the designed RBE, can accurately and rapidly distinguish internal and external faults.

title: Fréchet Power-Scenario Distance: A Measure for Evaluating Synthetic Data Across Multiple Time-Scales in Smart Grids
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence models for smart grids have advanced rapidly in recent years, and the synthetic data they produce can help mitigate limited data access caused by strict confidentiality constraints in power systems. A central challenge, however, is how to rigorously evaluate the quality of both the generative models and the synthetic time series they produce. Generic evaluation metrics are often not tailored to grid-specific requirements—such as multi-timescale temporal structure, cross-resolution consistency, and physically meaningful operating regimes—and therefore can yield misleading assessments. In this work, we propose a novel measure based on the Fréchet Distance (FD) estimated between two datasets in a power-centric learned feature space. Our approach embeds smart-grid time series using a hierarchical multi-resolution encoder trained on real grid data that encourages sensitivity to multi-timescale dynamics and resolution-consistent operational signatures. Across multiple use cases, the resulting Fr’echet Power-Scenario Distance (FPD) exposes temporal and physical mismatches more reliably and correlates with downstream task performance more strongly than conventional baselines, enabling more robust benchmarking of generative models for smart-grid data.

title: Adaptive Fast Clearing Algorithm Based Peer-to-Peer Transaction for Microgrid-integrated Distribution Network Considering Uncertainty
abstract: Peer-to-peer (P2P) transaction has become an effective way to improve the economic efficiency of microgrids (MGs). However, existing studies neglect the impacts of electricity power-carbon-green certificate join cost (PCGC), energy-reserve co-optimization and uncertainty within MG on P2P transactions schemes. To fill this gap, this paper proposes a P2P transaction framework for interconnected MG, where carbon allowance-green certificate constraints, reserve constraints, joint chance constraints are employed respectively to capture PCGC coupling, reserve provisioning, and uncertainty impacts. An optimization-based piecewise-linear marginal utility function (MUF) is developed to characterize MG's price-responsive behaviors under multi-resource coordination. Furthermore, an adaptive fast clearing algorithm (AFCA) is designed with a network-fee-exempt non-iterative clearing scheme and a network-fee-incorporated oscillation-resistant iterative scheme to ensure computational efficiency and distribution network security. Numerical results demonstrate that the MUF effectively captures the impacts of internal reserve, network constraints, risk preference, and PCGC on inter-MG P2P trading behaviors. The AFCA significantly accelerates computation, with a 97.72% time reduction compared to the widely used alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) in a 5-MG system, and solves the 20-MG system in only 1.45 s with an optimality error of merely 0.59%.

title: Zero-Shot Nonintrusive Load Monitoring via Contrastive Learning-Based Multiscale Dual-Path Temporal Fusion Network
abstract: Nonintrusive load monitoring (NILM) aims to disaggregate household power usage into individual appliance consumption, enabling efficient demand management. However, existing models struggle with scenarios where only aggregate power sequences are available in the target domain without any individual appliance labels for fine-tuning (i.e., zero-shot), which causes significant performance degradation and limits their practical applicability in real-world scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose a novel model named contrastive learning-based multiscale dual-path temporal fusion network (CL-MDTFN). CL-MDTFN integrates an energy-aware subsampling embedding block for multiscale feature extraction and a residual power decoupling block for capturing both fine-grained transient activities and overarching load trends. By leveraging the autocorrelation contrastive loss, CL-MDTFN effectively learns the long-term variations of the signals, enabling accurate load disaggregation in unlabeled households. Experiments on U.K.-DALE and REDD demonstrate that CL-MDTFN outperforms existing NILM models in fully labeled and unlabeled scenarios.

title: Situationally Aware Rolling Horizon Multi-Tier Load Restoration Considering Behind-The-Meter DER
abstract: Restoration in power distribution systems (PDSs) is well studied, however, most existing research focuses on network partition and microgrid formation, where load transfer is limited to adjacent feeders. This focus is not practical, as when adjacent feeders lack sufficient capacity, utilities may request support from more distant feeders in practice. Such a hierarchical restoration is complex, especially when involving changing system conditions due to cold load pickup and delayed reconnection of behind-the-meter DERs. To fill this research gap, a situationally aware multi-tier load restoration framework is proposed. Specifically, models are proposed to describe the multi-tier load restoration, including the multi-tier load transfer and substation transformer and feeder protection models. By introducing binary actional switching variables and load block transfer variables, the models effectively captures the dynamics of switches and multi-tier transfer process. To integrate situational awareness of evolving system conditions, the problem is formulated as a mixed-integer linear program (MILP) and then embedded within a rolling horizon optimization. Particularly, a set of safeguarded constraints are developed based on segment-level restoration reward bounds to mitigate the myopia of traditional rolling horizon optimization. The proposed safeguarded rolling strategy guarantees that each time step is lower bounded by a (1 − ε)-fraction of its optimal restoration potential, thereby balancing short-term switching decisions with long-term restoration goals. Finally, cases studies on the modified IEEE 123-node test feeder validate the proposed multi-tier restoration framework.

title: Topology and Parameter Joint Identification in Imbalanced Low-Voltage Distribution Networks Based on Load Characteristic Propagation
abstract: Low-voltage distribution networks often suffer from incomplete or outdated network records, making it challenging to obtain the topology and line parameters under actual operating conditions. To address this issue, a joint identification method is proposed based on the propagation of load transient characteristics. First, the principle of load characteristic propagation is elaborated, and the concept of coupling impedance is introduced. Second, a set of linear regression equations is established based on the changes in current and voltage of the terminal measurements before and after load switching, and then these equations are solved using the least squares method to form the coupling impedance matrix. Finally, a node recursive algorithm is applied to iteratively derive the network topology and calculate line parameters in a bottom-up manner. Case studies show that by effectively extracting the information contained in the transient measurement dataset, the proposed method can correctly identify the network topology and accurately estimate line parameters even under three-phase imbalanced conditions, providing high practical value for engineering applications.

title: Post-Quantum Cyber Risk Assessment for Networked Microgrids: A Unified Framework
abstract: The growing interconnection of microgrids enhances the efficiency and resilience of modern power systems, yet it also increases exposure to cyber threats. The emergence of quantum computing further compromises traditional security methods, creating an urgent need for post-quantum risk assessment strategies. This paper presents a unified framework for evaluating both classical and post-quantum cyber risks in networked microgrids. In the proposed approach, each microgrid is represented in a multidimensional feature space, from which a single system matrix model is constructed to capture network-wide characteristics. The matrix model enables statistical, structural, temporal, and cryptographic authenticity checks, while deviations are quantified through a unified threat score and an associated confidence score. Extensive case studies demonstrate the performance of the framework under different cases. The results highlight its value as a methodological advance for systematically assessing post-quantum cyber risks in networked microgrids and for supporting their secure transition into the quantum era.

title: Consistent Power System Time Series Imputation via Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
abstract: In power systems, particularly in smart grids and advanced metering infrastructure, multivariate time-series data are essential monitoring indicators. However, missing data often arise from limitations in data acquisition equipment, communication failures, and extreme weather conditions. This issue significantly affects downstream tasks, especially in critical applications like power load forecasting and demand response. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a time-series imputation method based on diffusion probabilistic models, called Diff-TSI. By introducing a structure-consistency-guided strategy during the sampling phase, Diff-TSI significantly improves imputation performance, particularly under high missing rates. Specifically, Diff-TSI incorporates three structural constraints during data generation. First, the stable low-frequency characteristics of power time series are utilized to construct a dataset-level magnitude-frequency template and define an online frequency-domain consistency score. Through monotonicity detection based on EMA and path-level resampling, the low-frequency spectral drift of the sampling trajectory is suppressed. Second, a noise-aware time-varying temporal consistency constraint mechanism is proposed, which couples residual correction and gradient-based guidance with noise standard deviation scheduling, gradually aligning the sampling trajectory with the true data distribution without requiring extensive manual hyperparameter tuning. Finally, a second-order difference smoothing term is applied at the sample boundaries to alleviate structural discontinuities in the transition regions. Extensive experiments on multiple real-world datasets show that Diff-TSI consistently outperforms state-of-the-art imputation methods under various missing rates and patterns, demonstrating strong robustness. Notably, the study focuses on missing-data imputation under normal operating conditions, while fault or anomaly scenarios remain beyond the scope and will be investigated in future work.

title: Real-Time Charging Control for Electric Roadways
abstract: This paper studies the optimal wireless charging for electric vehicles (EVs) driving through an electric roadway (ER). We first develop a clairvoyant formulation to model and optimize the minute-level energy transmission between the ER and EVs, which incorporates ER microgrid operation, EV-side power balance, battery dynamics, and wireless power transfer limits as constraints. However, this formulation requires future information regarding how EVs will be driven, which is often unavailable during real-time operation. To circumvent the dependence on future information, we design a causal algorithm by leveraging the optimality of valley-filling charging profiles of the clairvoyant formulation. We theoretically establish the optimality of the proposed algorithm in an ideal setting without considering losses. The algorithm is then extended to account for practicalities such as estimation errors, losses, and incorporation of a stationary battery co-located with the ER. Finally, for distinct traffic conditions, we numerically validate the performance of the algorithm under realistic settings (incorporating losses) with different information patterns (with and without lookahead).

title: A Magnetically Integrated Adaptive Fault Current Limiter for Low-Voltage DC Distribution Systems
abstract: Low-voltage direct current (LVDC) distribution system facilitates the efficient integration of renewable energy sources (RESs) and various DC loads. However, it is susceptible to DC faults due to the mismatch between the VSC blocking time and the tripping time of DC circuit breakers (DCCBs). To this end, this paper proposes the magnetically integrated adaptive fault current limiter (MIAFCL) for LVDC distribution systems, which resolves two major issues in current research: (i) inadequate adaptability to changing operational conditions, and (ii) incompatibility in space-constrained installation scenarios. First, a novel fault current limiter topology is presented, and the stage-topology adaptive adjustment mechanism is developed to make it exhibit low intervention under normal conditions and effective current limitation during fault events. Subsequently, a high- and low-frequency reactor integration scheme for MIAFCL based on non-orthogonal decoupling method is proposed. This scheme mitigates core saturation, improving current-limiting performance and significantly enhancing component integration. Additionally, a detailed parametric design approach is proposed for the magnetic integration and circuit configuration of the MIAFCL. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method are validated through simulation and experimental verification, as well as comparisons with existing studies.

title: Anchor Graph-Based Subspace Clustering for Large-Scale Residential Load Profiling
abstract: Residential load profiling clustering is crucial for optimizing energy use and enhancing efficiency of power distribution system. However, current methods face three limitations like reliance on manual similarity measures, high computational costs, and inflexibility to new load profiles. To address these challenges, this letter proposes a large-scale anchor graph-based subspace clustering method for residential load profiling. Specifically, the distance matrix is directly learned from the load profile through subspace clustering to handle high-dimensional data and uncover hidden load patterns. Then, an anchor graph is constructed to capture the intrinsic structure of the learned subspace, which can effectively reduce the computational complexity. Finally, k-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) is adopted to assign labels to new load profiles based on selected anchor points, eliminating the need for re-clustering the entire dataset. Tests on real-world London household data confirm the method’s effectiveness and efficiency. The code is available at https://github.com/U-T-G/AGSC

title: A Smoothing Pseudo-Labeling Framework for FDIA Detection under Large Load Integration
abstract: Real-world cyber intrusions, such as the 2022 Ukraine power-grid attack, have underscored the vulnerability of modern smart grid operation. While deep learning has exhibited promise in false data injection attack (FDIA) detection, its reliability is often compromised by evolving grid conditions, especially those driven by large load integration. Such substantial load variations alter the statistical characteristics of operational patterns, rendering existing FDIA detectors ineffective. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a Smoothing Pseudo-Labeling (SPL) framework. SPL utilizes a fine-tuning mechanism to efficiently transfer diagnostic knowledge from historical operational patterns to new scenarios. Specifically, the framework integrates pseudo-labeling to leverage unlabeled data from new environments, while applying label smoothing regularization on labeled samples to mitigate overfitting and enhance robustness against noisy predictions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework adapts effectively to dynamic grid environments. SPL achieves detection performance comparable to state-of-the-art benchmarks while requiring only 10% of the labeled data and 42.62% of the training time.

title: Real-Time Operation of Electric Autonomous Mobility-on-Demand System Considering Power System Regulation
abstract: Electric autonomous mobility-on-demand (EAMoD) systems are emerging all over the world. However, their potential swarm charging in depots may deteriorate operation of the power system, further in turn affecting EAMoD system’s optimal operation. To prevent this latent risk, we develop a real-time coordination framework for the EAMoD system and the power system. First, the temporal-spatial characteristics of EAMoD fleets are fully described based on a Markov decision process model, including serving trips, repositioning, and charging. Second, charger accessibility of EAMoD depot charging is well modeled as real-world configuration, wherein fast and slow charge piles are both included. Third, the power system regulation model provides real-time charging regulation constraints for EAMoD systems to prevent potential overload and undervoltage. To address the poor solution quality attributed to the complex decision space of the EAMoD system, this paper proposes a piecewise linear-based approximate dynamic programming algorithm combined with model predictive control. Numerical experiments in the Manhattan and a 14-node power distribution network validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm and underscore the necessity of system coordination.

title: Coordinated Load Frequency Control for Multi-Frequency Oscillations in Wind-Pumped Storage Hybrid Microgrids
abstract: Hybrid microgrids (MGs), particularly those incorporating wind power and pumped storage, have been widely adopted for renewable energy generation. However, hydraulic characteristics of pumped storage units (PSUs) and inter-generator interactions induce inevitably multi-frequency oscillations during load frequency control (LFC). To capture these oscillation behaviors and achieve effective suppression, this paper proposes a coordinated LFC strategy for hybrid MGs that integrates high-fidelity system modeling. A novel distributed frequency response (DFR) model is developed that incorporates hydraulic states (e.g., pressure heads in complicated pipelines and surge tank water levels) and network topology, offering improved accuracy over conventional average system frequency (ASF) models. Based on this model, a multi-input multi-output model predictive control (MIMO-MPC) scheme is designed to track the power allocation setpoint and enable wind turbines to participate in LFC in coordination with synchronous generators. Simulation results on 6-bus and IEEE 39-bus systems demonstrate the proposed strategy’s superiority in frequency regulation. Under variable wind conditions, it reduces the integral of time-weighted absolute error (ITAE) of frequency deviation for the PSU by 47.3% compared to the PI control. These outcomes validate the enhanced transient performance and robustness of the scheme for practical smart grid applications.

title: Advanced Zero-Dynamics Attacks on Hydroelectric Systems: A Data-Driven Stealth Approach
abstract: The integration of networked control systems in power generation has significantly increased the susceptibility of hydroelectric systems to cyber-physical attacks. Among these, zero-dynamics attacks (ZDAs) are particularly concerning because they can disrupt system stability by manipulating control inputs. These attacks are designed to operate covertly, avoiding detection through system outputs. However, current ZDA methods often fall short in maintaining the level of stealth necessary for complete concealment. To overcome this limitation, we introduce an enhanced ZDA approach that leverages data-driven methods alongside tensor regression to improve both concealment and disruptiveness. Injecting carefully crafted attack signals into system inputs can destabilize the system’s internal state without causing detectable anomalies in the outputs. In addition, to counter the enhanced ZDA, we propose a dual-layer detection mechanism. This mechanism embeds an adaptive watermark in the system inputs, utilizes a Kalman filter to predict the actual outputs, and ultimately employs a chi-square detector to identify the ZDA.

title: A Blockchain-Based Federated Learning Approach for Electricity Theft Detection through Dual-Verification
abstract: Malicious clients participating in data collection and interaction may launch attacks such as model and data poisoning to degrade the performance of the global model and conceal their electricity theft behaviors. Although existing studies have introduced blockchain technology to achieve decentralization, they still suffer from limited pre-aggregation validation dimensions. To address these issues, this paper proposes a blockchain-based federated learning approach with dual-verification (BFL-DV) for electricity theft detection. In the pre-aggregation stage, a multi-metric reputation-based consensus committee verification strategy is designed, which effectively mitigates the impact of malicious participants. In the post-aggregation stage, a dynamic threshold-based blockchain verification strategy is developed to counter security risks during the transmission process, which can refuse malicious global updates adaptively. Experimental results demonstrate that BFL-DV can accurately reduce the impact of all malicious clients under the data poisoning attack. Notably, across various proportions of malicious clients, the proposed framework achieves an average AUC improvement of 32.68% compared with SOTA methods, demonstrating its consistent performance advantage.

title: Fairness and Voltage Quality Enhancement through Active-Reactive Dynamic Operating Envelopes in Unbalanced Low-Voltage Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel fairness-aware dynamic operating envelope (DOE) framework for equitable active and reactive power allocations in unbalanced low-voltage (LV) networks with high penetration of distributed energy resources (DERs). The proposed method extends proportional fairness from conventional active power definitions to apparent power, allowing customers constrained in active export to contribute via reactive power support. A multi-phase current–voltage optimal power flow (OPF) formulation is developed, incorporating inverter capability constraints, transformer loading limits, and voltage unbalance factor (VUF) mitigation. The VUF is explicitly regularised to address phase-level voltage quality issues arising from asymmetric DER installations and single-phase connections. Time-series simulations on a real-world Australian LV feeder demonstrate that the proposed Fair (P,Q) DOE with explicit VUF regularisation consistently maintains transformer and voltage constraints, reduces VUF below industry guidelines, and improves both fairness and network utilisation compared to existing methods. Results confirm that integrating reactive power flexibility and unbalance-aware fairness metrics enables a more inclusive and power-quality-compliant operation of DER-rich LV networks.

title: Optimal Power Allocation Strategy for Hydrogen Production System of ALK-PEM Electrolyzer Considering Second-level Response Characteristics
abstract: Most electrolyzer scheduling models operate at minute-to-hour resolutions and thus overlook the second-level dynamics required to track fast renewable fluctuations, leading to avoidable wind curtailment and revenue loss for off-grid wind-to-hydrogen systems. This paper proposes an optimal power allocation framework for a hybrid electrolyzer system composed of alkaline (ALK) and proton exchange membrane (PEM). ALK provides low-cost, large-capacity baseline production but responds slowly, whereas PEM delivers second-level agility to absorb high-frequency power variations. A two-stage strategy is designed to couple efficiency-oriented power allocation with refined power dynamic regulation under explicit start/stop, ramp-rate, and capacity constraints. Moreover, a dual-layer array-rotation mechanism is incorporated to balance operating stress across stacks and prevent unit-specific overuse. Case studies using measured data from a practical project in Northeast China show that, compared with traditional power allocation methods, the proposed method increases hydrogen production by 3.3%-5.6%, reduces wind curtailment by 70.6%-94.7%, and improves hydrogen revenue by 21.9%-32.0%, enhancing renewable utilization and profitability.

title: Correlation-Exploiting False Data Injection Attack and Corresponding DRL-Based Detection Countermeasure in Partially Observable Grids
abstract: In partially observable power grids, limited knowledge of grid topology and correlated nodal injections presents significant challenges to cybersecurity, complicating the development of stealthy false data injection attacks (FDIAs). To address these issues, this paper proposes an optimization-based and correlation-aware FDIA that remains stealthy under AC state estimation and bypasses bad data detection (BDD) by explicitly incorporating spatio-temporal dependencies among nodal injections. The attack strategy employs a reduced-dimensional measurement matrix and an error covariance matrix to model injection correlations, thereby minimizing operational constraint violations. Correspondingly, a coupled Cubature Kalman Filter approach is characterized to enhance state estimation accuracy and reduce conservatism. To counter such evolving attacks, a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based detection mechanism is developed. Extensive validation on IEEE 14, 30, 57, and 118-bus systems demonstrates the effectiveness and robustness with 99.92%-100% accuracy of the proposed method.

title: ViT4LPA 2.0: A Smart Meter Pre-Trained Vision Transformer for Aggregated-Level Load Disaggregation
abstract: Pre-trained neural networks have significantly advanced machine learning, enhancing performance and reducing reliance on labeled datasets. In this study, we analyze a pre-trained neural network trained with residential smart meter load data and its transferability for aggregated-level load profile analysis. This study introduces ViT4LPA 2.0, a pre-trained hierarchical vision transformer (H-ViT) tailored for load profile analysis. ViT4LPA 2.0 is adapted for heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) load disaggregation at an aggregated-level, leveraging knowledge from individual smart meter load profiles. The H-ViT model employs a window self-attention mechanism to capture both local and global features. Pre-training is performed using masked image modeling on 2,000 smart meter load profiles, followed by domain adaptation and fine-tuning with limited labeled data. Extensive simulations demonstrate the model’s effectiveness, achieving approximately 5% daily accumulated error on aggregated-level load disaggregation with less than 15% HVAC consumption visibility in residential households. The model significantly outperforms state-of-the-art benchmarks, showing a 20–35% performance improvement. Additionally, a comprehensive sensitivity analysis and interpretability study provide insights into hyperparameter selection and the model’s decision-making process.

title: Distribution-Level Local Imbalance Market for Multi-Timescale Settlement and Network-Constrained Balancing
abstract: Existing local energy markets (LEMs) and local flexibility markets (LFMs) in distribution systems are primarily designed to facilitate energy trading and alleviate congestion. However, they lack explicit mechanisms for modeling nodal power deviations, pricing marginal imbalance costs, and allocating fast frequency response. This paper proposes a local imbalance market (LIM) that introduces a node-level imbalance formulation and distribution locational imbalance prices (DLIPs), internalizing network constraints and the balancing costs induced by power imbalances. The LIM incorporates a multi-timescale clearing structure where the distribution system operator (DSO) computes minute-level balancing decisions and DLIPs. A frequency response sensitivity matrix (FRSM) allocates second-scale fast-response costs to the nodes that caused the deviations. A native ADMM-based LIM clearing algorithm is designed to achieve scalable, privacy-preserving coordination among prosumers, aggregators, and the DSO without revealing private information. The second-scale allocation algorithm ensures cost causality and budget consistency through real-time measurement and expost reconciliation. Case studies on three modified distribution networks demonstrate that the proposed LIM enhances balancing efficiency, preserves participant privacy, and achieves accurate cost attribution under renewable uncertainty. The LIM provides a practical and economically consistent pathway for integrating renewable-rich resources into distribution-level market operations.

title: Coordinated and Generalizable Planning and Operation of PV-Storage-Charging Facilities in Coupled Power and Transportation Nexus
abstract: Transportation electrification, driven by large-scale electric vehicle adoption, is pivotal to global decarbonization. However, rapid charging infrastructure deployment entails high urban investment costs, risks of local grid overloads, and challenges to renewable integration due to temporal mismatches between charging demand and generation. Photovoltaic– storage–charging (PSC) stations provide a promising solution, yet coordinated planning of coupled transportation and power distribution networks (CPTN) remains underdeveloped. Existing models rarely integrate charging price signals, and analytical or heuristic approaches for hierarchical optimization under multi-scale uncertainties and nonlinear dynamics remain computationally prohibitive. This paper proposes a hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for coordinated PSC planning and operation in CPTN. A multi-time-scale nested optimization model is formulated as a Markov Game with options, enabling collaborative learning of long-term investment and short-term pricing and dispatching policies. Spatial–temporal graph convolutional networks capture dynamic nodal and edge features, while a proximal policy optimization scheme with advantage decomposition and sequential updates enhances perception and convergence. Case studies based on real-world settings demonstrate superior performance against state-of-the-art benchmarks in terms of policy quality, computational and convergence efficiency, while revealing significant cost-efficiency improvements and operational benefits for CPTN.

title: A Bi-Level Trading and Correction Strategy for Electricity–Carbon Emission Right–Renewable Energy Certificate Coupled Market Considering Power Flow Constraints
abstract: Driven by “dual carbon” goals and stricter distribution-network (DN) security constraints, designing a multi-park electricity–carbon emission right–renewable energy certificates (ECR) coupled trading mechanism that ensures carbon reduction, high renewable energy integration and compliance with power flow constraints has become a pressing issue. This paper develops a bi-level coupled ECR trading and correction framework for day-ahead market (DAM) that accounts for the information barrier between levels, with integrated energy systems (IESs) as core participants. In the lower level, a peer-to-peer (P2P) trading mechanism based on asymmetric Nash bargaining (ANB) theory is developed for ECR coupled day-ahead trading market, which can capture the coexistence of diverse low-carbon indicators in the current trading environment and drive the IESs toward eco-economic operation. In the upper level, a multi-stakeholder-oriented correction strategy for ECR coupled day-ahead trading is established to mitigate potential power flow violations and inter-temporal violation transfers, which consists of a single-period correction strategy that consider both fairness and economic efficiency, and a flexible time window-based correction strategy under multi-period coupling. Through illustrative examples, the superiority of the proposed method is verified in terms of enhancing prosumer profits, reducing carbon emissions, promoting renewables utilization, and ensuring power-flow constraints with faster inter-level convergence.

title: Time-invariance of distribution system security region considering flexible resources
abstract: Distribution system security region (DSSR) has time-variant characteristics after considering flexible resources (FRs) such as energy storage systems and demand response. This paper conducts an in-depth study on the time-variance of DSSR for the first time, pointing out and addressing the problem it causes. Firstly, the existing DSSR model is introduced. The reason for the time-variance is analyzed: FR regulations are reflected in the region varying. The problem caused by the time-variance of DSSR is also analyzed, namely that the region-based method will lose its speed advantage in online security analysis. Secondly, a time-invariant DSSR model and its security analysis method are proposed, considering complete types of FRs and N-1 security. The key to addressing the time-variance of DSSR is to reflect FR regulations as the operating point movement. Finally, the proposed model and method are verified in a real case and a large case, and compared with the existing research. The comparison shows that the proposed model maintains the speed advantage of the region-based method in security analysis. This work establishes a link between time-variant DSSR and time-invariant DSSR, laying a key foundation for practical applications of DSSR in smart distribution networks.

title: A Bi-Level Distributed Framework for Hierarchical Coordination of Multiple Agents’ Flexibility Under Uncertainty of Flexibility Requirements
abstract: This paper presents a market-based hierarchical framework to coordinate joint energy and flexibility capability trading in a day-ahead market, while considering real-time flexibility adjustment to cover uncertainties in forecasted flexibility requirements, using an adaptive robust optimization (ARO) method. In this regard, a two-stage model is presented; in the first stage, the agents’ energy and flexibility capabilities and the distributed energy resources’ commitments are optimized to meet the forecasted flexibility requirements. In the second stage, the agents’ flexibility is adjusted to cover the worst-case uncertainty realization in the net load variations. In the proposed framework, a technical virtual power plant (TVPP) operates a local market in the distribution network which is cleared in coordination with the wholesale market. In this model, a deregulated environment is addressed in which the agents’ hierarchical interactions and their preferences are captured using a bilevel problem with multiple lower levels. To solve the problem, the ARO problems are solved using the column-and-constraint generation (CCG) algorithm. Moreover, the bilevel problem is solved according to the agents’ hierarchical transactions using a distributed iterative approach. Implemented case studies and numerical results demonstrate the model’s effectiveness and show that the framework ensures full flexibility requirement coverage under all uncertainty levels.

title: Scalable Building HVAC Control Through Laxity-Based Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Demand flexibility is playing a vital role in maintaining grid power balance, reducing peak demand, and saving energy bills. Given their highly shiftable characteristics and significant contribution to a building’s energy consumption, Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) systems can provide valuable demand flexibility to the power systems by adjusting their power consumption in response to electricity price and power system needs. To exploit such flexibility in terms of both operation time and demand level, modeling and efficient aggregation techniques of HVAC load flexibility are investigated in this paper. To tackle the curse of dimensionality issue associated with an increasing number of HVAC devices, the notion of laxity for HVAC is proposed in this work to quantify the urgency level of each building’s operation request. Considering the inherent complexity and uncertainty presented in HVAC systems, we design a novel deep reinforcement learning (RL)-based controller to schedule the aggregate dispatched power based on the efficient representation of aggregated laxity information as well as the electricity price. For each HVAC load, only laxity information is revealed instead of full states, and integrated with proposed RL agent using least-laxity-first (LLF) rule for power allocation. To validate the superior efficiency and performance provided by our laxity-based RL agent, we evaluate the temperature control and the energy cost savings of a large number of HVACs in both single-zone and multi-zone scenarios under varying climate and electricity market conditions. Our data-driven approach also significantly saves the modeling and data burden compared to model-based controllers. Empirically, numerical results also indicate that the proposed approach outperforms standard RL with full HVAC states. Compared to the widely used deep RL baseline, it achieves up to 42% reduction in total energy cost while maintaining comparable average temperature deviation.

title: TFDA: A Time-Frequency Domain Adaptive Model for Multi-Source Multi-Task Anomaly Detection and Localization in Distribution Systems
abstract: Accurate anomaly detection and localization in distribution systems enable the timely event identification and the implementation of appropriate response strategies, which could minimize potential damage. However, many existing methods rely on extensive sensor data, requiring comprehensive measurement variables for data preprocessing and fusion, which limits their applicability in real-world scenarios. Moreover, prior methods often lack the necessary adaptive mechanisms to account for the variability of anomalies, which lead to inconsistent performance across tasks. To address these challenges, we propose a data-driven time-frequency domain adaptive model (TFDA) that incorporates both time-domain and frequency-domain features, only utilizing voltage magnitudes. The model introduces a spatial patch embedding block, which integrates sensor spatial information as graph priors and processes time-series data through patch-based operations to mitigate the impact of multi-resolution data. In the frequency-domain block, an adaptive thresholding technique is applied to eliminate less informative parts of the frequency spectrum. In the time-domain block, an adaptive weighting is utilized to balance the contributions of interchannel and intra-channel anomaly information. We perform simulations on hardware-in-the-loop testbed to generate data that closely approximates real-world scenarios and demonstrate the superiority of our method over the baseline.

title: Low Carbon Scheduling of Integrated Energy System Based on Large Language Model-Embedded Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: The complex multi-energy coupling characteristics inherent to integrated energy system (IES) present unprecedented challenges for the implementation of low-carbon scheduling. Existing optimization methods often exhibit limitations in system scalability, algorithm adaptivity, and carbon reduction efficacy for complex IES. This paper proposes a Large Language Model (LLM)-Embedded Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (LEMARL) to address the aforementioned issues. The proposed method integrates the global perception capability of LLMs with the dynamic optimization capability of MARL. Specifically, the LLM-Embedded module generates high-quality reward functions and policy frameworks from a global perspective, while the MARL module leverages these LLM-generated strategies for distributed interactive iterations—greatly enhancing computation efficiency and scalability. Simulation results demonstrate that LEMARL reduces carbon emissions by 7.76% and simultaneously decreases operating costs by 4.49% in a small-scale IES. Furthermore, LEMARL also exhibits superior applicability and scalability in large-scale IES of the IEEE 141-bus power grid integrated with 51-node thermal system.

title: Data-Driven Privacy-Preserving Modeling and Frequency Regulation with Aggregated Electric Vehicles via Bilinear Hidden Markov Model
abstract: Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology allows bidirectional power flow for real-time grid support, making electric vehicles (EVs) well-suited for ancillary services such as frequency regulation. However, existing methods for flexibility estimation and coordinating aggregated EVs often rely on individual EV traveling information (e.g., arrival/departure time) and/or characteristic parameters (e.g., charging efficiency, battery capacity) as well as real-time state-of-charge (SOC), which raises privacy concerns and faces data quality issues. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a data-driven, privacy-preserving modeling and control framework for frequency regulation using aggregated EVs. The proposed method can provide accurate estimation for power outputs and flexibility of aggregated EVs and carry out effective frequency regulation without any individual EV information. Simulation results validate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method, which also outperforms the model-based and federated learning-based method under SOC data inaccuracies.

title: Andronov-Hopf Oscillator Based Harmonic Elimination Scheme for Grid-Connected Inverters
abstract: Conventional harmonic elimination methods for Grid-Connected Inverters (GCI) rely on individual harmonic extraction and compensation, resulting in increased complexity and slow dynamic response. In this paper, the Virtual Oscillator based Harmonic Compensation (VO-HC) is proposed. It uses the Andronov–Hopf oscillator not for synchronization or grid-forming purposes, but to extract the fundamental component from the distorted grid current. The Hopf oscillator is inherently frequency-adaptive, allowing it to extract the fundamental component and attenuate harmonics with negligible phase delay compared to traditional filters. The extractor provides unity-gain fundamental tracking even under frequency deviations and weak-grid conditions. The extracted fundamental is then subtracted from the measured grid current to isolate the grid current harmonics. These harmonics are compensated using a simple proportional compensator loop in the stationary frame as a feedforward, operating in parallel with a conventional Synchronous Reference Frame (SRF) current controller. This results in fast low-order harmonic compensation of grid current, improving the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) of the GCI system. Experimental results demonstrate THD reduction from up to 18.4% to below 2.5%, with a transient settling time of approximately 2–3 ms. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through both simulation and experimental results conducted on a laboratory two-inverter microgrid setup under distorted and weak-grid conditions.

title: Robust Unknown Input Observer based Estimation and Mitigation against Sensor Spoofing Attacks in Cyber-Physical Microgrids
abstract: Microgrids are increasingly dependent on real-time sensing and network communication for the monitoring and control of distributed energy resources (DERs), exposing them to numerous cyber attacks such as sensor spoofing. In such attacks, additive biases are injected into sensor measurements without directly spoofing the communication network and control logic. Conventional observer-based bias estimation methods face several challenges. They typically rely on accurate system models, and their estimation performance deteriorates in the presence of system uncertainties, including parameter uncertainties, process and measurement noise, and unknown inputs. These factors make sensor spoofing-induced biases difficult to distinguish from normal state variations, causing interaction between sensor biases and system uncertainties and leading to degraded control performance in practical microgrid operation. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a Robust Unknown Input Observer (RUIO) for the accurate estimation of sensor spoofing-induced biases in the presence of various system uncertainties. The sensor bias is modeled as an augmented state, and the observer gain is synthesized using Linear Matrix Inequality (LMI) optimization under an H∞ performance criterion to ensure robustness against system uncertainties. Given the structural observability limitation of the Unknown Input Observer (UIO) formulation, which prevents simultaneous estimation of independent current and voltage sensor biases, an event-triggered bias estimation and mitigation framework is designed to counter any single sensor spoofing attack. The dual-RUIO scheme is switched adaptively based on the current-sharing error after mitigation, with an appropriate holding interval in place to ensure stable operation. The effectiveness of the proposed RUIO-based framework is validated through extensive experiments on a cyber-physical microgrid testbed. Comparative evaluations against conventional state estimation methods demonstrate improved estimation accuracy and mitigation performance.

title: Trajectory-Independent Flexibility Envelopes of Energy-Constrained Systems With State-Dependent Losses
abstract: As non-dispatchable renewable power units become prominent in electric power grids, demand-side flexibility appears as a key element of future power systems’ operation. Power and energy bounds are intuitive metrics to describe the flexibility of energy-constrained loads. However, to be used in operation, any power consumption trajectory fulfilling the power and energy bounds must necessarily fulfill the load’s constraints. In this paper, we demonstrate that energy bounds defined as the minimum and maximum energy consumption potential of a load with state-dependent losses are Trajectory-Dependent (TD), i.e., for any energy value in the bounds a feasible power trajectory exists, but not all power trajectories enclosed in the energy envelopes satisfy the load’s constraints. To guarantee the satisfaction of load constraints for all trajectories, we define Trajectory-Independent (TI) energy bounds. We present TI envelope formulations for individual loads, as well as physically coupled loads and assess the proposed formulations in a building heating system, a system with state-dependent losses. We find that using a TD envelope as energy bounds in operation may yield room temperature up to  $3.3~^{\circ }$ C higher and  $3.4~^{\circ }$ C lower than admissible. Overall, poorly insulated buildings observe a TI energy envelope that differs significantly from their TD envelope.

title: Multi-time Scale Distributed Stochastic Economic Dispatch for Flexible Traction Power Supply System
abstract: Flexible traction power supply system (FTPSS), integrated with renewable energy, energy storage, and power flow controllers (PFC), offers great potential for safe and economical railway operation. However, the uncertainty in traction load and photovoltaic (PV) output poses significant challenges to cost-effective dispatch. Therefore, a multi-time scale distributed stochastic economic dispatch method for FTPSS is proposed. The prediction module uses LSTM to produce point forecasts, while KDE models the forecast errors to construct predictive intervals and generate scenarios for PV output and traction load. A stochastic programming model is then formulated, where uncertainties in traction load and PV are represented by chance constraints and scenarios. In the first stage, the day-ahead forecast is used to solve the stochastic optimization model to minimize daily operational cost. In the second stage, the scheduler uses the day-ahead plan as a soft reference and reoptimizes at each rolling step with updated probabilistic forecasts, implementing only the first control move to maintain real-time responsiveness and economic efficiency. The optimization model is solved using an ADMM-based distributed algorithm, which accounts for limited inter-subsystem communication and reduces computational complexity. A case study based on a real electrified railway demonstrates that the proposed method improves economic performance by reducing operating costs by approximately 9% under uncertainty.

title: An Autonomous Identification and Mitigation Scheme for Man-in-the-Middle Attacks on Microgrid Secondary Control Signals
abstract: In centralized microgrids, secondary control signals are transmitted from the microgrid central controller (MGCC) to each distributed energy resource (DER) to restore voltage and frequency. However, these signals remain vulnerable to cyber attacks. Unlike unidirectional attacks, such as false data injection and denial-of-service attacks, Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacks enable bidirectional manipulation of both uplink and downlink communications, making detection and mitigation at the MGCC extremely challenging. To address these practical challenges, a novel autonomous identification and mitigation scheme is proposed in this paper for centralized microgrids, utilizing only the local measurements from each DER. In this scheme, each DER independently determines whether it is under attack by analyzing the trajectories of local measurements and calculated values at the point of common coupling. The attack signals are then reconstructed with the attack frequency and amplitude components estimated via Fast Fourier Transform and least squares estimation. Subsequently, the attacked DER implements mitigation actions by injecting the inverse of the reconstructed attack signals back into the local controller. Compared to existing schemes, the proposed scheme 1) utilizes local measurements only, enhancing resilience against MITM attacks in centralized microgrids; 2) identifies specific attacked secondary control signals; and 3) reconstructs and mitigates complex attack waveforms without relying on additional trustworthy communication links. The proposed scheme is evaluated in MATLAB/Simulink, with simulations confirming its effectiveness in identifying and mitigating MITM attacks.

title: Nonlinear Arc High Impedance Grounding Fault Feeder Dynamic Visualization Detection in Active Distribution Networks
abstract: Arc high impedance fault is the main fault in active distribution network, but the fault characteristics are weak and the influence of nonlinear transition resistance make the fault difficult to detect. The detection method based on the dynamic trajectory between characteristic signals is not affected by arc distortion and has good anti-interference performance. However, the existing ignores the influence of parameter asymmetry and damp rate, and the selected characteristic signals have low content in arc high impedance fault. To eliminate the influence of nonlinear arc and further improve the accuracy of detection, a novel AHIF dynamic detection is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the equivalent circuit model considering parameter asymmetry and damp rate is established to obtain the precise analytical expressions of transient zero-sequence voltage, transient zero-sequence current, and transient inductive current flowing through arc suppression coil. Secondly, the dynamic trajectories between transient zero-sequence voltage and transient zero-sequence current and between transient inductive current and transient zero-sequence current are analyzed respectively to visualize the weak fault characteristic. Finally, the faulty feeder selection method is proposed based on the movement trend of dynamic trajectory between transient inductive current and transient zero-sequence current. Simulation and 10kV experimental platform prove the feasibility of the proposed methods.

title: Research on Protection Method for DC Distribution Networks Based on Fault Current Energy Peak-to-Average Ratio
abstract: Existing protection methods for DC distribution networks suffer from limitations such as low transition resistance tolerance, noise susceptibility, and inadequate speed. To overcome these challenges, this paper first establishes a bipolar short-circuit fault model that considers multi-converter interactions. Based on this model, we reveal the intrinsic relationship between fault current energy distribution and fault conditions, and propose a novel protection criterion utilizing the Energy Peak-to-Average Ratio (EPAR) of the fault current. By converting the time-domain waveform characteristics of the fault current into energy distribution features, the method effectively characterizes the influence of transition resistance on fault characteristics, enabling rapid and reliable identification of high-impedance bipolar short-circuit faults. An adaptive collaborative protection method leveraging the complementary characteristics of EPAR and current variation is developed. By constructing a dual-criterion coordination mechanism integrating current variation and EPAR, this method enables dynamic setting and complementary identification, ensuring full-line rapid protection for internal bipolar faults. Furthermore, the impact of setting value selection on protection reliability and sensitivity was quantitatively analyzed, constraints in the protection setting process were elucidated, and a theoretical basis for applying the proposed method to DC distribution networks with different structures was provided. A 10 kV multi-terminal flexible DC distribution network model incorporating diverse converters is built in PSCAD/EMTDC to validate the proposed method under various fault conditions. Simulation results demonstrate that the method accurately discriminates faults within 1.5 ms after occurrence, achieves transition resistance tolerance up to  $100~\Omega $ , and exhibits strong noise immunity.

title: Hybrid Islanding Detection Based on Voltage THD and Non-Power Frequency Impedance in Inverter-Interfaced Microgrid
abstract: Unintentional islanding detection is a critical requirement of an inverter-interfaced microgrid in order to apply an appropriate control and protection scheme and to avoid unsynchronized reclosure. The existing passive methods mainly use the voltage and frequency signals for islanding detection, but they are highly dependent on power mismatch and hence have a large non-detection zone (NDZ). The active methods have low NDZ, but they compromise power quality due to continuous injection of a perturbation signal through inverters. For reliable and fast islanding detection with negligible power quality impact, a new two-layer hybrid technique combining a total harmonic distortion (THD) based passive method and a non-power frequency impedance measurement based active method is proposed in this work. In the first layer, voltage THD is used to suspect an islanding condition, based on which the active method in the second layer is initiated. The active method injects a non-power frequency perturbation signal through the inverter control and then measures the impedance at that frequency. The proposed method declares the islanding event once the impedance measurement exceeds a threshold value. The method is tested and validated on standard IEEE 1547 test system for several islanding and non-islanding events to demonstrate its efficiency.
